title: 478. The French Revolution: Showdown in Versailles (Part 4)

sentences.en: They hit at seven o'clock in the morning of the 13th of July, hit hard, hailstones big as eggs.
sentences.zh: 他们在7月13日早晨七点发起袭击，攻势猛烈，冰雹大如鸡蛋。

sentences.en: According to some reports, they were as big as bottles, chunks of ice, as hard as diamonds, weighing a pound and a half.
sentences.zh: 据一些报道称，它们有瓶子那么大，是一块块坚硬如钻石的冰块，重达一磅半。

sentences.en: A hailstone that was weighed in one village outside Paris came to eight pounds.
sentences.zh: 巴黎郊外一个村庄里称过的一块冰雹重达八磅。

sentences.en: One weighed in another village came to ten.
sentences.zh: 另一个村庄称过的一块重达十磅。

sentences.en: The stones broke windows, smashed tiles on roofs, raised fields, destroyed vineyards, stripped bare fruit trees, struck horses dead.
sentences.zh: 这些冰雹砸碎了窗户，击碎了屋顶的瓦片，毁坏了田地，摧毁了葡萄园，剥光了果树的树皮，将马匹当场击毙。

sentences.en: And even killed some peasants who were preparing to harvest what had promised to be an excellent crop of wheat.
sentences.zh: 甚至还砸死了几位正在准备收割有望获得大丰收的小麦的农民。

sentences.en: That is Robert Darnton in his wonderful book, The Revolutionary Temper.
sentences.zh: 这段话出自罗伯特·达恩顿在他那本精彩的著作《革命情绪》中的描述。

sentences.en: And he is describing the storm that hit France in the summer of 1788.
sentences.zh: 他描述的是17世纪80年代（注：原文1788）夏天袭击法国的那场风暴。

sentences.en: And Dominic, we do love a storm, a gathering storm on the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们确实热爱风暴，一场蓄势待发的风暴，接下来的事情就顺理成章了。

sentences.en: But I mean, you could argue that this is possibly the most significant actual non-metaphorical storm in the whole of European history.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，你完全可以说，这可能是整个欧洲历史上最具意义的实际而非隐喻的风暴。

sentences.en: You absolutely could, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以这么说，汤姆。

sentences.en: One would be quite justified in arguing that.
sentences.zh: 这样争论是完全合情合理的。

sentences.en: So purely in its own terms, it's quite an extraordinary event, meteorological event.
sentences.zh: 所以，仅就其本身而言，这是一场相当非凡的事件，一场气象事件。

sentences.en: It sweeps all the way across France from Rouen, Normandy, all the way down to Toulouse and the Long Dock.
sentences.zh: 它从诺曼底的鲁昂一直席卷整个法国，直到图卢兹和朗格多克。

sentences.en: There was a Scottish gardener, a great gardening writer and gardening expert called Thomas Blakey, who was traveling in France in 1788.
sentences.zh: 当时有一位苏格兰园丁，他是一位伟大的园艺作家兼园艺专家，名叫托马斯·布莱基，他于1788年正在法国旅行。

sentences.en: And he said that the hailstones were so monstrous, so enormous, that the countryside was littered with dead hares and dead partridges.
sentences.zh: 他说，这些冰雹太巨大、太庞大，以至于乡村田野到处都是死野兔和死鹧鸪。

sentences.en: It wiped out budding vines in Alsace, Burgundy and the Loire, laid waste to wheat ripening in the fields of the Oligny, pitted young apples in the Calvado,
sentences.zh: 它摧毁了阿尔萨斯、勃艮第和卢瓦尔河谷初绽的葡萄藤，糟蹋了奥利尼田野里正在成熟的小麦，在卡尔瓦多斯砸伤了幼小的苹果，

sentences.en: shriveled young olives and oranges in the Midi.
sentences.zh: 让米迪地区的幼小橄榄和橘子干瘪枯萎。

sentences.en: What I like about that is that, actually, that was Robert Darnton.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这一点的原因是，实际上，那是罗伯特·达恩顿的话。

sentences.en: That was a quote from Robert Darnton.
sentences.zh: 那是引自罗伯特·达恩顿的话。

sentences.en: It wiped out budding vines in Alsace, Burgundy and the Loire.
sentences.zh: 它摧毁了阿尔萨斯、勃艮第和卢瓦尔河谷初绽的葡萄藤。

sentences.en: Okay, we don't need it again.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们不需要再重复一遍了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: But anyway, yes, it's a terrible, it's a terrible storm.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，是的，这是一场可怕的风暴，一场可怕的风暴。

sentences.en: And of course, if you've been listening to the series, which we hope you have,
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你一直在收听这个系列节目，我们希望你确实听了，

sentences.en: you will know that it strikes at the worst possible moment when France is gripped by this political and financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 你就会知道，它在法国陷入这场政治和财政危机最糟糕的时刻给予了致命一击。

sentences.en: And the storm is then followed by a drought, so a drought across France, then suddenly a very hot summer.
sentences.zh: 风暴过后接着是一场旱灾，全法国都遭遇旱灾，随后紧接着是一个非常炎热的夏天。

sentences.en: And farmers are writing to the court in Versailles sending letters asking for help.
sentences.zh: 农民们纷纷写信给凡尔赛宫廷，发信请求援助。

sentences.en: A once ravishing countryside has been reduced to an arid desert.
sentences.zh: 曾经迷人的乡村如今已沦为一片荒凉的沙漠。

sentences.en: And there's a real sense of kind of catastrophe, which, of course, in the context of everything that we were talking about in the last episode.
sentences.zh: 那种真正的灾难感油然而生，当然，这在我们上一集讨论的所有背景之下也是如此。

sentences.en: Not helpful, is it?
sentences.zh: 这可真帮不上忙，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's not helpful at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也帮不上忙。

sentences.en: The interesting thing, actually, is that last time we were talking about the Ancien Régime, how the stereotype of it is so misleading.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有趣的是，上一次我们讨论旧制度时，发现关于它的刻板印象是多么具有误导性。

sentences.en: And so it is with this case.
sentences.zh: 这次的情况也是如此。

sentences.en: You would think, if you had read A Tale of Two Cities and all of the sort of, you know, you used the caricatures of the French Revolution and the French elite,
sentences.zh: 如果你读过《双城记》以及所有那些，你知道的，你所了解的关于法国大革命和法国精英阶层的种种讽刺画像，你可能会认为

sentences.en: that nobody did anything to help.
sentences.zh: 没有人做任何事情来提供帮助。

sentences.en: And you would be wrong.
sentences.zh: 那你就大错特错了。

sentences.en: Because actually, the Archbishop of Paris launches this big charity drive.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上，巴黎总主教发起了一场大规模的慈善募捐活动。

sentences.en: The king gives a million livres, even though, you know, the monarchy has pretty much run out of money.
sentences.zh: 国王捐出了一百万里弗，尽管你知道，君主制基本上已经花光了所有的钱。

sentences.en: A national lottery is organised and it raises 12 million livres to pay for relief.
sentences.zh: 全国上下组织了一场彩票抽奖，筹集了1200万里弗用于救灾。

sentences.en: But as we will see, it is not remotely enough to rescue the situation because, Tom, nature has more storms in store.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们将要看到的，这远远不足以挽救局势，因为，汤姆，大自然还酝酿着更多的风暴。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: Wow.

sentences.en: So the elements are combining against the monarchy.
sentences.zh: 所以各种自然因素正在联合起来对抗君主制。

sentences.en: They are indeed.
sentences.zh: 它们确实如此。

sentences.en: And the Ancien Régime is in a mess, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 而且旧制度已经陷入了一团糟，我认为这样说并不过分。

sentences.en: Were you trying to think of a meteorological metaphor for this?
sentences.zh: 你刚才是在试图为这个局面想一个气象隐喻吗？

sentences.en: No, I've moved on from the meteorological metaphors.
sentences.zh: 不，我已经不再使用气象隐喻了。

sentences.en: I was maybe thinking of a building one.
sentences.zh: 我可能在考虑一个关于建筑的隐喻。

sentences.en: I was thinking perhaps it's tottering on its foundations.
sentences.zh: 我在想，也许它正摇摇欲坠。

sentences.en: It is tottering on its foundations.
sentences.zh: 它的确已经摇摇欲坠了。

sentences.en: Because as we discussed at the end of the last episode,
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们在上一集末尾所讨论的，

sentences.en: something looking very much like a French Revolution has already broken out in Grenoble and in Dauphiné in the southeast of France and has spread to other provinces.
sentences.zh: 法国东南部格勒诺布尔和多菲内已经爆发了极像法国大革命的事件，并且已经蔓延到其他省份。

sentences.en: Louis XVI in desperation has announced that he will call the estates general.
sentences.zh: 路易十六在绝望中宣布他将召开三级会议。

sentences.en: And we ended last time with the bombshell that Archbishop Brienne, the finance minister, has basically declared bankruptcy, at least partial bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集结束时留下了一个重磅消息：财政大臣布里讷总主教基本上已经宣布破产，至少是部分破产。

sentences.en: And it's ironic, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这不是很具有讽刺意味吗？

sentences.en: Because he doesn't believe in God, but all these acts of God have now hit France.
sentences.zh: 因为他不相信上帝，但所有这些天灾现在却接二连三地降临到法国。

sentences.en: Yes, ironically.
sentences.zh: 是的，真具讽刺意味。

sentences.en: Well, he didn't believe in the deficit.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他不相信赤字的存在。

sentences.en: And then he was pointed to the books.
sentences.zh: 然后有人把账本指给他看。

sentences.en: He's on a learning curve.
sentences.zh: 他正在经历一个学习的过程。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: Yeah.

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: Well,

sentences.en: his learning curve is abruptly terminated a week later on the 25th of August when he is booted out and the monarchy turned to the one person who everybody in France thinks can rescue the situation.
sentences.zh: 他的学习过程在一周后的8月25日戛然而止，当时他被赶下台，君主制转向了全法国都认为能够拯救局势的那个人。

sentences.en: This is a man we mentioned very briefly last time.
sentences.zh: 这个人我们在上一次简要提到过。

sentences.en: His name is Jean-Jacques Necker.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫让-雅克·内克尔。

sentences.en: And he is not a courtier.
sentences.zh: 他不是朝臣。

sentences.en: He is not an aristocrat.
sentences.zh: 他不是贵族。

sentences.en: He is not even French.
sentences.zh: 他甚至都不是法国人。

sentences.en: He is a Swiss Protestant from a Geneva banking family.
sentences.zh: 他是一个来自日内瓦银行世家的瑞士新教徒。

sentences.en: And he is meant to be the great financial whiz kid of Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 他被认为是西欧伟大的金融神童。

sentences.en: Because the Swiss, even then, have a kind of reputation for sobriety and the kind of man that you would trust to sort out your bank balance.
sentences.zh: 因为即使在当时，瑞士人也有一种务实稳重的声誉，是那种你可以放心把银行存款托付给他们的人。

sentences.en: Totally, they do.
sentences.zh: 完全同意，它们会的。

sentences.en: Necker is a, it seems odd now from our perspective, all these centuries later, to comprehend how a Swiss banker could be such a folk hero across France.
sentences.zh: 内克尔竟然能成为全法国的平民英雄，从我们如今这些世纪之后的视角来看，似乎显得有点不可思议。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 对，我知道。

sentences.en: But absolutely, there was a sense in France in the late 18th century that Protestants, although they are weird, alien and heretical,
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，在18世纪末的法国，人们有一种感觉：新教徒虽然有些奇怪、格格不入且离经叛道，

sentences.en: are nevertheless very boring and they can be trusted.
sentences.zh: 但他们却非常乏味，而且是可以信任的。

sentences.en: They're kind of black sober suits.
sentences.zh: 他们就像是那种穿黑色素服、严肃刻板的人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: Exactly.

sentences.en: All that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So when I was reading up on Necker, I was reminded of how a lot of people in Britain thought about the Canadian national banker, Mark Carney.
sentences.zh: 所以当我阅读关于内克尔的资料时，我想起了许多英国人对加拿大国家银行行长马克·卡尼的看法。

sentences.en: A listener to the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 一个《历史其余部分》的听众。

sentences.en: A listener to the rest is history, exactly.
sentences.zh: 一个《历史其余部分》的听众，没错。

sentences.en: Who ran the Bank of England.
sentences.zh: 他曾掌管英格兰银行。

sentences.en: And there was a perception, I think, in Britain that he was very measured, very Canadian, very kind of controlled and kind of apparently very sober.
sentences.zh: 我想，在英国人眼中，他非常审慎、极具加拿大风格，非常克制，而且表面上看起来非常严肃稳重。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not saying he wasn't sober.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我并不是说他不稳重。

sentences.en: What are you saying, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你到底想说什么？

sentences.en: The avoidance of doubt.
sentences.zh: 免得引起误解。

sentences.en: That's how he appeared.
sentences.zh: 他给人的印象就是这样。

sentences.en: If he's listening, Dominic is not accusing you of being a drunk.
sentences.zh: 如果他在收听的话，多米尼克可不是在指控你是个酒鬼。

sentences.en: No, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 不，我不是。

sentences.en: But I'm saying people attributed him, people who knew nothing about Mark Carney, precisely because he was an outsider, not tainted by British politics.
sentences.zh: 但我想说的是，人们将各种品质赋予了他——那些根本不了解马克·卡尼的人，仅仅因为他是一个局外人，没有受到英国政治的污染。

sentences.en: People attributed him with sort of extraordinary powers.
sentences.zh: 人们认为他具备某种非凡的力量。

sentences.en: And they saw him as a figure who represented stability and solidity.
sentences.zh: 他们将他视为一个代表着稳定与坚实的人物。

sentences.en: And also neutrality.
sentences.zh: 还有中立性。

sentences.en: Yeah, neutrality, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，中立性，完全正确。

sentences.en: And objectivity, not having too many vested interests.
sentences.zh: 还有客观性，没有太多的既得利益。

sentences.en: And I guess that that's why people think, you know, Necker is a deus ex machina.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是为什么人们会觉得，你知道的，内克尔就像是一个从天而降的救星。

sentences.en: They do, indeed.
sentences.zh: 它们确实如此。

sentences.en: He's someone who can be introduced to kind of cut through all the Gordian knots that have been strangling the French economy.
sentences.zh: 他是一个可以被引进，来斩断那些一直勒紧法国经济的重重乱麻的人。

sentences.en: We love it.
sentences.zh: 我们很喜欢。

sentences.en: We love it.
sentences.zh: 我们很喜欢。

sentences.en: I mean, not just one Gordian knot, according to you, but multiple Gordian knots.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，根据你的说法，不只是一个乱麻，而是多个乱麻。

sentences.en: All of them.
sentences.zh: 全部都是。

sentences.en: And Necker, to be fair, is brilliant at, I mean, the one thing he had done is he'd got loans for the American war, you might argue, with disastrous consequences.
sentences.zh: 说句公道话，内克尔确实非常擅长——我的意思是，他做过的一件事就是为美国战争筹集了贷款，你也可以说，这带来了灾难性的后果。

sentences.en: He's very good at getting loans because he has so many friends in the banking business.
sentences.zh: 他在筹集贷款方面非常在行，因为他在银行业有那么多朋友。

sentences.en: So as soon as he arrives, he says, I can do what Brienne could not.
sentences.zh: 所以他刚一到任就说，布里埃纳做不到的事，我能做到。

sentences.en: I can get my friends to lend you money at decent rates.
sentences.zh: 我可以让我的朋友们以优惠的利率借钱给你们。

sentences.en: I will be able to tide us over for at least another year until the estates general can meet and we can actually sort this thing out.
sentences.zh: 我们至少能撑过一年，直到三级会议召开，我们真正把这事解决掉。

sentences.en: And perhaps set up some new constitutional body or whatever it might be that will approve taxes.
sentences.zh: 或许还能建立某种能够批准税收的新宪政机构，或者诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: And so the stock exchange, which had been very jittery in the summer of 1788, kind of returns to normal.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1788年夏天曾一度非常焦虑不安的股票市场，又恢复了正常。

sentences.en: And there's a sense, you know, maybe we've got a bit of direction.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，你知道的，也许我们找到了一点方向。

sentences.en: Maybe we've got a bit of calm.
sentences.zh: 也许我们有了一点平静。

sentences.en: But I think that sense, Tom, would be illusory.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这种感觉将是虚幻的，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, because surely people know that there's an absolute catastrophe looming because the hailstones have wiped out the wheat harveSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为大家肯定都知道一场绝对的灾难即将来临，因为冰雹摧毁了小麦收成。

sentences.en: They do indeed.
sentences.zh: 它们确实如此。

sentences.en: And that, of course, has terrible implications for bread.
sentences.zh: 这当然对面包产生了可怕的影响。

sentences.en: It does indeed.
sentences.zh: 它确实如此。

sentences.en: There is a sense, I think, that all the time something is simmering.
sentences.zh: 我想，人们能感觉到某种情绪一直在暗中酝酿。

sentences.en: So when Brienne fell, there were celebrations in Paris that turned into rioting.
sentences.zh: 所以当布里埃纳下台时，巴黎爆发了庆祝活动，并演变成了骚乱。

sentences.en: There was fighting between the Paris watch and these celebrators stroke rioters.
sentences.zh: 巴黎巡警和这些庆祝兼骚乱的人群之间发生了冲突。

sentences.en: Perhaps 20 people were killed in the fighting.
sentences.zh: 冲突中大约有20人丧生。

sentences.en: I mean, this is fighting with kind of, this is your classic kind of, the watch have sabers and bayonets.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种冲突带有某种典型色彩，这是你们那种典型的冲突，巡警手持军刀和刺刀。

sentences.en: By the end, they're firing into the crowds.
sentences.zh: 到了最后，他们开始向人群开枪。

sentences.en: Soldiers restore order in the capital eventually.
sentences.zh: 军队最终恢复了首都的秩序。

sentences.en: But exactly as you say, because of the storms, everybody knows that something very bad is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，由于暴风雨的缘故，每个人都知道将有非常糟糕的事情发生。

sentences.en: And the reason is this thing about bread.
sentences.zh: 原因就在于面包这件事。

sentences.en: You know, it's the classic thing in the French Revolution is that you get great hordes of people chanting for bread.
sentences.zh: 你知道，法国大革命中经典的场景之一，就是大批民众高呼着要面包。

sentences.en: That's one of the kind of images.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种标志性的画面之一。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is that three out of four people in France subsist almost entirely on a, basically, a particular kind of loaf, which is called the four-pound loaf.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，法国四分之三的人口几乎完全靠一种特定的面包维生，基本上被称为四磅装的面包。

sentences.en: And you need, if you've got a family of four, you need two of these loaves every day to feed them.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个四口之家，你每天需要两个这种面包来养活他们。

sentences.en: Now, one loaf costs eight sous.
sentences.zh: 现在，一个面包售价八苏。

sentences.en: And Emmanuel Labourer makes about 25 sous a day.
sentences.zh: 而一个普通体力劳动者一天的收入大约是二十五苏。

sentences.en: So, in other words, he will be spending half, maybe more than half of his daily income on these two loaves of bread.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他要花掉一半甚至超过一半的日收入来买这两个面包。

sentences.en: And if the bread prices rise, he's in a real mess.
sentences.zh: 如果面包价格上涨，他就陷入了真正的困境。

sentences.en: So, by October, the price has already gone from eight to 12 sous.
sentences.zh: 所以到十月份，价格已经从八苏涨到了十二苏。

sentences.en: And eventually, as we will see, it will peak at about 15 sous.
sentences.zh: 最终，正如我们将看到的，价格将达到约十五苏的峰值。

sentences.en: And it peaks, doesn't it, on the 14th of July, 1789?
sentences.zh: 而且它在1789年7月14日达到顶峰，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, 14th of July, 1789, day of the fall of the Bastille.
sentences.zh: 对，1789年7月14日，巴士底狱陷落之日。

sentences.en: Now, you could say, I mean, there's nothing anyone can do about this.
sentences.zh: 现在你可能会说，我的意思是，对此谁也无能为力。

sentences.en: This is a complete act of God.
sentences.zh: 这是一场纯粹的天灾。

sentences.en: You know, the storms have destroyed the harveSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，暴风雨毁了庄稼。

sentences.en: There are not enough crops, not enough wheat.
sentences.zh: 农作物不够，小麦不够。

sentences.en: There's not going to be enough flour.
sentences.zh: 面粉将不够用。

sentences.en: There's not going to be enough bread.
sentences.zh: 面包也将不够吃。

sentences.en: Prices will rise.
sentences.zh: 价格将会上涨。

sentences.en: But this is an age of pamphlets and of rumours and therefore of conspiracy theories, right?
sentences.zh: 但这是一个充满小册子、谣言以及阴谋论的时代，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: Exactly.

sentences.en: And so, if something bad happens, someone must be to blame.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有什么坏事发生，一定有人该承担责任。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: Exactly.

sentences.en: That's exactly it.
sentences.zh: 完全就是这样。

sentences.en: Ever since the whole issue was opened by Calon, and obviously, in many ways, going back even further, there has been this rhetoric of the king's ministers.
sentences.zh: 自从卡洛纳挑起整个问题以来，显然在很多方面，甚至还要追溯到更早，就一直有一种国王大臣的论调。

sentences.en: The king's ministers who are despotic and they don't care and they just want to trample on our ancient liberties and all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 国王的大臣们专横跋扈，他们毫不在乎，只想践踏我们古老的自由，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And now people start to say, well, this is all the fault of the king's ministers.
sentences.zh: 现在人们开始说，嗯，这都是国王大臣们的错。

sentences.en: They're not giving us any relief.
sentences.zh: 他们没有给我们提供任何救济。

sentences.en: They're probably hoarding grain themselves, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，他们自己可能还在囤积粮食。

sentences.en: They're probably profiting from all this and driving prices up.
sentences.zh: 他们可能从中牟取暴利，推高了物价。

sentences.en: Only the estates general can save us.
sentences.zh: 只有三级会议才能拯救我们。

sentences.en: And then if that's not bad enough, I promised you that nature had more tricks up her sleeve,
sentences.zh: 如果这还不够糟糕的话，我向你们保证，大自然还有别的花招没使出来呢，

sentences.en: Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆。

sentences.en: On the 26th of November, 1788, there is an unexpected snowfall.
sentences.zh: 1788年11月26日，天降一场意料之外的大雪。

sentences.en: Basically, winter has come unexpectedly heavily and unexpectedly early.
sentences.zh: 基本上，冬天来得出人意料地猛烈，出人意料地早。

sentences.en: And this kicks off what Robert Danson describes as the longest, cruelest, coldest winter that anybody in France had ever known.
sentences.zh: 这就拉开了罗伯特·丹森所描述的法国人经历过最漫长、最残酷、最寒冷的冬天的序幕。

sentences.en: So, by December, Paris is completely covered with snow.
sentences.zh: 所以，到了十二月，巴黎完全被积雪覆盖了。

sentences.en: So, the Seine is frozen over.
sentences.zh: 塞纳河也结冰了。

sentences.en: People are walking on the Seine.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至能在塞纳河上行走。

sentences.en: There are frozen bodies lying in the streets.
sentences.zh: 街头躺着冻僵的尸体。

sentences.en: By New Year's Eve, the temperature has fallen to the lowest ever recorded in France, minus
sentences.zh: 到了除夕夜，气温降至法国有记录以来的最低点，零下

sentences.en: 10 degrees Fahrenheit.
sentences.zh: 10华氏度。

sentences.en: The rivers are all frozen.
sentences.zh: 所有的河流都结冰了。

sentences.en: Of course, the rivers being frozen means that the water mills, they can't create flour.
sentences.zh: 当然，河流结冰意味着水磨无法运转来磨面粉。

sentences.en: The rivers are frozen.
sentences.zh: 河流结冰了。

sentences.en: The roads are snowbound.
sentences.zh: 道路被大雪封锁。

sentences.en: They cannot transport supplies of bread to those areas that are suffering the moSt.
sentences.zh: 他们无法将面包供应运送到那些受灾最严重的地区。

sentences.en: And the snow is everywhere in France.
sentences.zh: 大雪覆盖了法国各地。

sentences.en: It's as far south as the Languedoc in the southweSt.
sentences.zh: 远在西南部的朗格多克也未能幸免。

sentences.en: And it falls pretty much every other day between February and April 1789.
sentences.zh: 在1789年2月到4月之间，几乎每隔一天就会下一场雪。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a real freak winter.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个真正的反常寒冬。

sentences.en: And so, they must all be sitting in Versailles looking out of the window thinking, oh no.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们肯定都坐在凡尔赛宫里向窗外张望，心里想：哦，不。

sentences.en: Completely they are.
sentences.zh: 完全是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, because they're getting reports all the time that basically there's a lot of people
sentences.zh: 对，因为他们不断收到报告，说基本上有很多人

sentences.en: in France who are kind of labourers with no land and they rely on seasonal work and they're all out of work and they're just starving.
sentences.zh: 在法国，他们算是没有土地的零工，依赖季节性工作谋生，现在全都失业了，正在挨饿。

sentences.en: You know, they have no money, they have no food.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们没有钱，没有食物。

sentences.en: And dying, presumably.
sentences.zh: 大概还在死去吧。

sentences.en: And dying, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，也在死去。

sentences.en: The majority of French men and women are peasant sharecroppers, smallholders.
sentences.zh: 大多数法国男女都是佃农或小农。

sentences.en: So, they work their land, they owe the seigneur, the local landowner, they owe him for goods and stuff and they owe him various exactions.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们耕种土地，欠着领主（当地地主）的债，他们欠地主的货物钱等等，还欠他各种苛捐杂税。

sentences.en: With this winter following on the storm, they probably won't be able to pay him what they owe.
sentences.zh: 在经历了风暴之后的这个冬天，他们很可能无力偿还债务。

sentences.en: This means that they will probably be evicted from their land and they will be demoted to the class of those people who have no land.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们很可能会被驱逐出土地，降为无地贫民阶层。

sentences.en: But at least they have the consolation of knowing that the seigneur doesn't have to pay taxes.
sentences.zh: 但至少他们可以聊以自慰的是，领主不用交税。

sentences.en: So, that must be a rule.
sentences.zh: 所以，这一定是个规矩。

sentences.en: Yeah, that the seigneur is fighting for the liberties of France.
sentences.zh: 对，领主是在为法国的自由而战。

sentences.en: Yeah, for the liberty of his right not to pay taxes.
sentences.zh: 对，为了他免交税收的自由。

sentences.en: Tom, I think it's fair to say that in general and the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得可以说，总的来说，剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: We deplore people who don't pay their rightful taxes, don't we?
sentences.zh: 我们谴责那些不依法纳税的人，对吧？

sentences.en: I think we do.
sentences.zh: 我想我们是的。

sentences.en: We set out our position a year ago in the series on the American War of Independence.
sentences.zh: 我们在去年关于美国独立战争的系列节目中就表明过立场了。

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.zh: 我们确实说过。

sentences.en: And we're sticking to it now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在依然坚持这一点。

sentences.en: Just pay your taxes for God's sake.
sentences.zh: 看在上帝的份上，按时交税吧。

sentences.en: French, American, what is wrong with you people?
sentences.zh: 法国人，美国人，你们到底怎么了？

sentences.en: But this is such a hostage to fortune when we get investigated by tax authorities.
sentences.zh: 但当我们受到税务机关调查时，这就成了送上门的把柄。

sentences.en: That's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, now, anyway, you have a flood of people moving into the cities, desperate for relief.
sentences.zh: 所以，不管怎样，现在有一大批人涌入城市，渴望得到救济。

sentences.en: But if they manage to get there through the snow, there is very little there for them.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们历经风雪赶到那里，会发现能得到的实在太少。

sentences.en: Because France already is suffering from quite high unemployment in the cities.
sentences.zh: 因为法国城市的失业率本来就已经相当高了。

sentences.en: Because, as we said right at the beginning of the last episode, the Ancien Régime is a modernising regime.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们在上一集开头所说的那样，旧制度是一个走向现代化的政权。

sentences.en: We're living in the age of the Industrial Revolution.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在工业革命的时代。

sentences.en: People are being, weavers, artisans, are being put out of work by machines, by capitalism.
sentences.zh: 织工、手工业者等人们正被机器、被资本主义夺去工作。

sentences.en: And by Britain.
sentences.zh: 还有英国。

sentences.en: And by Britain.
sentences.zh: 还有英国。

sentences.en: More specifically.
sentences.zh: 更具体地说。

sentences.en: Yeah, because Callon, who we wanted to liberalise the French economy, had signed, this is very Brexit negotiations, he'd signed a free trade deal with the British.
sentences.zh: 对，因为我们想要其自由化法国经济的卡洛纳曾签署过一份自由贸易协议，这非常像英国脱欧谈判，他与英国人签署了协议。

sentences.en: And he'd said, this will give us the shock we need, a bit of competition.
sentences.zh: 他还说过，这会给我们带来所需的冲击，带来一点竞争。

sentences.en: A bit of, you know, a spur to our economy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这有点像对我们经济的刺激。

sentences.en: A flood of British manufactured goods.
sentences.zh: 大批英国制造的商品涌入。

sentences.en: Yeah, cheap gloves and things.
sentences.zh: 对，廉价手套之类的东西。

sentences.en: Cheap gloves that are putting the French out of work.
sentences.zh: 正是这些廉价手套让法国工人失去了工作。

sentences.en: That's what my ancestors made in Derbyshire.
sentences.zh: 那正是我祖先在德比郡制造的东西。

sentences.en: They were making gloves.
sentences.zh: 他们当时就在做手套。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, basically, your ancestors were responsible for the Day of the Tiles in Grenoble.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，你的祖先要为格勒诺布尔的砖瓦日事件负责。

sentences.en: We played our bit.
sentences.zh: 我们也出了自己的一份力。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Tom, you kept that quiet during that whole incident, when 12-year-olds were being shot.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，在12岁的孩子被枪杀的那整个事件中，你竟然一直守口如瓶。

sentences.en: But now you bring it up.
sentences.zh: 但现在你却把它提出来了。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: I've actually forgotten about it.
sentences.zh: 我其实都把这事给忘了。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，这样啊。

sentences.en: That's the word.
sentences.zh: 真有你的。

sentences.en: That's even worse.
sentences.zh: 这就更过分了。

sentences.en: It's the indifference.
sentences.zh: 这就是冷漠。

sentences.en: It's the indifference to the suffering you've caused.
sentences.zh: 这是对你所造成的痛苦的冷漠。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, over the winter of 1788, about a fifth of the population of Paris are unemployed.
sentences.zh: 所以在1788年的冬天，大约五分之一的巴黎人口处于失业状态。

sentences.en: So, that's what, about 100,000?
sentences.zh: 那大概是多少，大约10万？

sentences.en: 100,000 people, yeah.
sentences.zh: 10万人，是的。

sentences.en: Well, or receiving relief of some kind, like poor relief.
sentences.zh: 好吧，或者说接受某种救济，比如贫民救济。

sentences.en: So, now we have the three ingredients that we talked about last time.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有了上次谈到的三个要素。

sentences.en: The political and financial crisis, the kind of high politics, the cultural moment, the cult of virtue, of passion, of living your truth, all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 政治和财政危机，也就是高层政治、文化氛围、崇尚美德与激情、活出自我真实的那一套东西。

sentences.en: And now the social unrest and the anger and the desperation.
sentences.zh: 还有现在的社会动荡、愤怒和绝望。

sentences.en: So, this is a lot of pressure on the estate general, which has been called and is supposed to resolve all this.
sentences.zh: 因此，这给三级会议带来了巨大的压力，三级会议已经被召集，本应解决这一切。

sentences.en: And the thing is, they've called the estate general, and it's going to meet the following spring, summer.
sentences.zh: 问题是，他们召集了三级会议，并将在第二年春夏季开会。

sentences.en: The date is a slightly movable feaSt.
sentences.zh: 具体日期是一个稍微可以变动的节日。

sentences.en: But they don't really know, as we said, what it is, how it will be arranged.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们所说，他们其实并不知道会议是什么样的，将如何安排。

sentences.en: There's no institutional memory of it, because it hasn't met since 1614, 15.
sentences.zh: 没有任何关于它的机构记忆，因为它自1614、15年以来就再没有召开过。

sentences.en: And the king has not decreed what it should be?
sentences.zh: 而且国王还没有颁布法令规定它该是什么样吗？

sentences.en: No, there's a flood of pamphlets.
sentences.zh: 没有，有大量的政治小册子涌现出来。

sentences.en: There's a huge sort of torrent of argument in the final months of 1788.
sentences.zh: 在1788年的最后几个月里，爆发了如潮水般的争论。

sentences.en: And what people want, if they are kind of reformers, they say the third estate, which is the commons, representing the great majority of the French people,
sentences.zh: 如果人们算作是改革派的话，他们想要的是第三等级，也就是平民，代表了绝大多数法国人民，

sentences.en: should absolutely not allow itself to be outvoted by the clergy and the nobility.
sentences.zh: 绝不能让自己在投票中被神职人员和贵族压倒。

sentences.en: So, the clergy are the first estate, nobles are the second estate.
sentences.zh: 所以，神职人员是第一等级，贵族是第二等级。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The mass of everybody else is the third estate.
sentences.zh: 其他广大民众都是第三等级。

sentences.en: Everybody else, yeah.
sentences.zh: 其他人，是的。

sentences.en: The third estate should have its numbers doubled, so it should be equivalent to those two.
sentences.zh: 第三等级的人数应该加倍，使其与前两个等级相当。

sentences.en: And they should all sit together so that a majority vote can decide all the big questions.
sentences.zh: 而且他们应该坐在一起开会，以便通过多数投票来决定所有重大问题。

sentences.en: That basically, it shouldn't be out.
sentences.zh: 基本上，就是不应该被排除在外。

sentences.en: Because even if its numbers are doubled, if it's outvoted by the other two chambers, if each chamber gets basically one vote, as it were, then they'll never be able to win.
sentences.zh: 因为即使人数加倍，如果它被其他两个议院在投票中击败，如果每个议院实际上只有一票的话，那么他们就永远无法获胜。

sentences.en: And can I ask, with all this talk about the general will of the people, which is already becoming very current,
sentences.zh: 请问，伴随着所有关于人民普遍意志的讨论——这已经变得非常普遍，

sentences.en: Is there already a sense that actually there shouldn't be three estates, there should just be the one national assembly which could speak and articulate the truth of the nation?
sentences.zh: 人们是否已经有一种感觉：事实上不应该有三个等级，而应该只有一个国民议会，它能够代表并表达国家的真相？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, what is the third estate, what is the third estate, which came out in January 1789?
sentences.zh: 那么，出版于1789年1月的《什么是第三等级？》是什么呢？

sentences.en: And it started with these famous words.
sentences.zh: 它以这句名言开篇。

sentences.en: We have three questions to ask.
sentences.zh: 我们有三个问题要问。

sentences.en: First, what is the third estate?
sentences.zh: 第一，什么是第三等级？

sentences.en: Everything.
sentences.zh: 全部。

sentences.en: Second, what has it been in the political order up to now?
sentences.zh: 第二，它迄今为止在政治体制中算什么？

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么都不是。

sentences.en: Third, what does it demand?
sentences.zh: 第三，它要求什么？

sentences.en: To become something.
sentences.zh: 成为某种存在。

sentences.en: So, this sort of idea that the third estate is everything.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种观点认为第三等级就是一切。

sentences.en: And he says, Sies, the third estate is a complete nation.
sentences.zh: 西哀耶斯说，第三等级是一个完整的国家。

sentences.en: He says there are 25 million of us.
sentences.zh: 他说我们有2500万人。

sentences.en: There are only 200,000 of them, nobles and priests.
sentences.zh: 贵族和神职人员只有20万。

sentences.en: We don't even need them.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至不需要他们。

sentences.en: He says, we are the nation.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们就是国家。

sentences.en: If we want a total reboot of France, we can have one.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想要对法国进行彻底的重启，我们就能做到。

sentences.en: If we lack a constitution, we must make one.
sentences.zh: 如果我们缺乏一部宪法，我们就必须制定一部。

sentences.en: The nation alone has that right.
sentences.zh: 只有国家才有这种权利。

sentences.en: I mean, he presumably, I mean, he's a member of the first estate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他大概……我的意思是，他本人是第一等级的成员。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we talked in the previous episode that there are nobles, members of the second estate, who sympathize with this.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集中谈到过，有些贵族——第二等级的成员——也对此表示同情。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That, you know, they would like to see their order, their estate dissolved into the entirety of a single assembly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们希望看到自己的等级融入到一个单一的议会中。

sentences.en: They absolutely would.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对是这么想的。

sentences.en: Yeah, they would.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们会的。

sentences.en: So, we'll see a very famous example in the Comte de Mirabeau, who is one of the most famous spokesmen for the third estate, but is a nobleman.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们将看到一个非常著名的例子，即米拉波伯爵，他是第三等级最著名的代言人之一，但他却是一位贵族。

sentences.en: And, of course, also the Duke of Orleans, who again we talked to, the cousin of Louis XVI, who, you know, is a member, obviously, of the second estate.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有奥尔良公爵，我们之前也讨论过他，他是路易十六的表弟，显然也是第二等级的成员。

sentences.en: Yeah, and actually, some of these people are very vitriolic about their own estates.
sentences.zh: 是的，事实上，这些人中有一些对他们自己的等级极其尖刻言辞激烈。

sentences.en: So, yes, an example.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，举个例子。

sentences.en: There's a real hint of menace in that pamphlet, what is the third estate?
sentences.zh: 在那本小册子《什么是第三等级？》中，有一种真正的威胁暗示。

sentences.en: He says, if the nobility and the clergy, like me, want to become part of the nation, they must discard their privileges.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果贵族和神职人员想像我一样成为国家的一部分，他们必须抛弃特权。

sentences.en: And he says, people are always asking what place should they occupy in the social order.
sentences.zh: 他还说，人们总是在问他们在社会秩序中应该占据什么位置。

sentences.en: He says, this is equivalent to asking what place should be assigned to a malignant disease which preys upon and tortures the body of a sick man.
sentences.zh: 他说，这就等于在问，应该给一种寄生在病人身体上并折磨病人的恶性疾病安排什么位置。

sentences.en: I mean, that analogy, your opponents are not even traitors, they are a disease.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种类比，你的对手甚至不是叛徒，他们是一种疾病。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very familiar, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对，这非常眼熟，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that is very familiar and very disturbing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这非常眼熟，也非常令人不安。

sentences.en: So, anyway, in this argument, Necker suggests a compromise, and he and the king issue a decision.
sentences.zh: 总之，在这场争论中，内克尔提出了一个妥协方案，他和国王共同做出了一项决定。

sentences.en: The third estate will get its key demand.
sentences.zh: 第三等级将达成其核心诉求。

sentences.en: It will get 600 deputies compared with the 300 or so for both the clergy and the nobility.
sentences.zh: 他们将获得600名代表，而教士和贵族各自只有大约300名。

sentences.en: Also, the third estate will be able to elect, choose its representatives, people like Siez, who come from the other estates.
sentences.zh: 此外，第三等级将能够选举和选择自己的代表，比如像西哀士这样来自其他等级的人。

sentences.en: So, if you're, Tom, a liberal reforming clergyman like him or a vicomte or whatever, and your own estate won't choose you, obviously,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你，汤姆，是一个像他那样支持自由改革的教士，或者子爵之类的人，而你所在的等级不选你，显而易见，

sentences.en: you could run in the third estate elections to get in that way.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过参加第三等级的选举来争取入选。

sentences.en: However, what Necker does not decide is whether the three estates are all going to sit together, which would allow the third estate to nominate,
sentences.zh: 然而，内克尔没有决定的是，这三个等级是否会坐在一起开会——这将允许第三等级进行提名，

sentences.en: or whether they would still be stratified kind of hierarchically and be in their different chambers.
sentences.zh: 还是他们仍然会按等级森严的阶层划分，分属不同的议事厅。

sentences.en: So, this kicks off these elections for the three estates, and they're very, very complicated, so let's try to steer clear of them as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就拉开了这三个等级选举的序幕，过程非常非常复杂，所以我们尽量少涉及为妙。

sentences.en: Basically, it's a filtration process.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是一个筛选的过程。

sentences.en: You've got a parish assembly, and then a district assembly, and then a provincial assembly.
sentences.zh: 你有一个教区议会，接着是区议会，然后是省议会。

sentences.en: It kind of varies from place to place, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这在每个地方似乎都不太一样，对吧？

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's all kind of random and very complicated.
sentences.zh: 这全都有点随机而且非常复杂。

sentences.en: And all the time, people have been encouraged.
sentences.zh: 而且在这期间，人们一直受到鼓舞。

sentences.en: And this is an amazing thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件了不起的事。

sentences.en: The king says to them, I want to hear all your grievances.
sentences.zh: 国王对他们说，我想听听你们所有的委屈。

sentences.en: I want to hear all your desires.
sentences.zh: 我想听听你们所有的诉求。

sentences.en: So, actually, the idea that the elite and the regime is totally indifferent and out of touch is not quite right.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，认为精英阶层和政权完全漠不关心、脱离实际的看法并不完全正确。

sentences.en: But this is the king.
sentences.zh: 但这毕竟是国王。

sentences.en: This is him playing his role of the father, the father of the nation.
sentences.zh: 这是他在扮演父亲的角色，也就是国父的角色。

sentences.en: Yeah, the patriot king.
sentences.zh: 没错，爱国国王。

sentences.en: Because, of course, I assume at this point, the implications of all this identification of the third estate with the voice of the people,
sentences.zh: 因为当然了，我猜在这个时候，将第三等级等同于人民呼声这一做法所带来的影响，

sentences.en: they're not yet discussing what implications that might have for the monarch.
sentences.zh: 他们尚未讨论这可能会对君主制产生什么影响。

sentences.en: No, because they're all, by the way, they're all monarchists.
sentences.zh: 没有，因为顺便说一句，他们全都是保王派。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, there is very little, certainly in the books that I've read, there's no mention of any overt republicanism at this stage.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，几乎没有——至少在我读过的书中——在这个阶段没有任何公开共和主义的提及。

sentences.en: Their dream, remember, a lot of these reformers is a British-style system, not an American republic.
sentences.zh: 记住，这些改革者的梦想是建立一个英国式的体制，而不是一个美洲共和国。

sentences.en: So, the ordinary people are composing these 25,000 dossiers, they could call them, in which they basically are saying, well, I don't like this tax,
sentences.zh: 所以，普通百姓正在撰写这大约25,000份档案，他们可以这样称呼它们，在这些档案中他们基本上是在说，嗯，我不喜欢这个税，

sentences.en: I don't like the seigneur does this, I would love to live with this or that or whatever this is.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢领主的这种做法，我希望过上这样或那样的生活，或者诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: But no one in Europe has ever, I think possibly in the world, has ever done an exercise like this before.
sentences.zh: 但欧洲——我想可能全世界——从来没有人做过这样前所未有的事情。

sentences.en: It is a monumental sort of public opinion survey.
sentences.zh: 这是一次划时代的民意调查。

sentences.en: And does it help stabilise the situation?
sentences.zh: 这有助于稳定局势吗？

sentences.en: Well, obviously the problem with it is that because it's unprecedented and extraordinary, it raises expectations no government, even a revolutionary government, can possibly meet.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，这里的问题在于，由于它史无前例且非同寻常，它抬高了期望值，以至于任何政府——甚至是革命政府——都根本无法满足。

sentences.en: Because people then, as now, they want impossible and contradictory things.
sentences.zh: 因为当时的人们和现在一样，想要一些不可能实现且相互矛盾的东西。

sentences.en: They want more food.
sentences.zh: 他们想要更多的食物。

sentences.en: They want more freedom.
sentences.zh: 他们想要更多的自由。

sentences.en: They want lower prices.
sentences.zh: 他们想要更低的物价。

sentences.en: They want less government on their backs and telling them what to do.
sentences.zh: 他们希望政府少管闲事，少对他们指手画脚。

sentences.en: They also want more government, a paternalistic government that is giving them, that is always there with relief and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们同时也希望有更多的政府介入，一个奉行家长制的政府，随时向他们提供救济以及诸如此类的援助。

sentences.en: They're asking things that no 18th century government can possibly supply.
sentences.zh: 他们提出的要求是18世纪的任何政府都绝对无法提供的。

sentences.en: And that will create, that's stoking their expectations to a pitch where the dissatisfaction will explode in fury and disappointment very shortly.
sentences.zh: 这将制造出——这正在将他们的期望推向一个高潮，用不了多久，不满情绪就会化为狂怒与失望彻底爆发。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, even as they are electing their representatives and drawing up their cahiers, the disorder in France is growing.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，就在他们选举代表并起草陈情书的同时，法国的社会动荡也在加剧。

sentences.en: And this is, again, this doesn't start with the revolution.
sentences.zh: 而且这也不是由革命开始的。

sentences.en: It precedes the revolution.
sentences.zh: 它发生在革命之前。

sentences.en: So effectively, I think what happens is the snow melts as the ice thaws and people go back to the streets.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，我认为发生的事情是随着冰雪消融，积雪融化，人们重新走上街头。

sentences.en: The food prices are still very high.
sentences.zh: 食品价格依然居高不下。

sentences.en: So the disorder returns to the streets and you get a series of reports by about March of food rioting across the country,
sentences.zh: 因此动荡重回街头，在大约3月份左右，你开始看到全国各地爆发粮食骚乱的报告，

sentences.en: all the way from France in the north to Avignon to Toulouse in the south.
sentences.zh: 从北部的法国一直延伸到阿维尼翁，再到南部的图卢兹。

sentences.en: And in particular, there is a sense that in the countryside, which is most of France, authority is really breaking down at this point.
sentences.zh: 特别是人们感觉到，在占法国大部分地区的农村，此时权威正在真正崩塌。

sentences.en: So I know we've both read Sharma's book.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道我们两个都读过夏尔马的书。

sentences.en: He has this wonderful section, doesn't he, where he introduces this by saying the first mass casualties of the French Revolution of France is rabbits.
sentences.zh: 他有一个非常精彩的章节，不是吗？他在其中引出这个话题时说，法国大革命、法国的第一批重大伤亡者是兔子。

sentences.en: Because he describes how people just, they're desperate.
sentences.zh: 因为他描述了人们是如何陷入绝望的。

sentences.en: They form platoons and they go out with guns or whatever, or bludgeons, like British schoolboys, and they're hunting game and rabbits and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们组成排，带着枪或者诸如此类的武器，或者拿着大棒，就像英国中学生一样，去猎取野味和兔子以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And this is in contravention of very restrictive game laws.
sentences.zh: 而这违反了极其严格的狩猎法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And actually, it's one of the stories of 1789, is the erosion of those game laws.
sentences.zh: 事实上，1789年的故事之一，就是那些狩猎法的瓦解。

sentences.en: And it's bad news for rabbits.
sentences.zh: 这对兔子来说可不是什么好消息。

sentences.en: And in a very short time, it will be bad news for birds.
sentences.zh: 而且在很短的时间内，对鸟类来说也不会是什么好消息。

sentences.en: Yeah, because when gamekeepers try to stop them and say, oi, this is the seigneur's stuff, they're just shooting them dead.
sentences.zh: 对，因为当看守试图阻止他们并说，喂，这是领主的东西时，他们直接就把对方给枪杀了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But you think the real victims in this are the birds, do you, Tom?
sentences.zh: 但你认为这里真正的受害者是鸟类吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: I do, really.
sentences.zh: 我确实这么认为。

sentences.en: Because they've remained the victims, because it becomes a kind of principle of, you know, the new order in France that you can kill as many birds as you like.
sentences.zh: 因为它们依然是受害者，因为这变成了一种原则——你知道的，法国新秩序的一项原则，即你可以随心所欲地杀鸟。

sentences.en: That François Mitterrand eating that bird.
sentences.zh: 就像弗朗索瓦·密特朗吃那只鸟一样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's a slippery slope from bread riots to François Mitterrand biting the head off an innocent bird.
sentences.zh: 从面包骚乱到弗朗索瓦·密特朗咬下一只无辜鸟类的头，这简直是一条滑向深渊的斜坡。

sentences.en: Oh, no, what a terrible image.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，多么可怕的画面。

sentences.en: So, there's a real sense of a power vacuum in the countryside.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们在农村确实感受到了一种权力真空。

sentences.en: People are attacking granaries and bakeries.
sentences.zh: 人们正在袭击粮仓和面包店。

sentences.en: Towns, unable to defend themselves of forming their own militias.
sentences.zh: 无法自卫的城镇开始组建自己的民兵武装。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, it's all kind of starting to crumble.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都开始分崩离析了。

sentences.en: But you know what you need in a situation like this?
sentences.zh: 但你知道在这种情况下一最需要什么吗？

sentences.en: Tell me.
sentences.zh: 告诉我。

sentences.en: You need a massive riot.
sentences.zh: 你需要一场大规模的暴动。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Dominic.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克。

sentences.en: Does such a thing happen?
sentences.zh: 这种事真的会发生吗？

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实发生了。

sentences.en: So, it happens in Paris.
sentences.zh: 所以它发生在巴黎。

sentences.en: And I think, again, I said in the last episode that the French Revolution started in Grenoble.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，正如我在上一集里所说，法国大革命始于格勒诺布尔。

sentences.en: You could also say it, I mean, if you want to choose an alternative date, it starts on the 28th of April, 1789, in Paris, not at the Bastille.
sentences.zh: 你也可以说——我的意思是，如果你想选一个替代的日期，它始于1789年4月28日的巴黎，而不是在巴士底狱。

sentences.en: So, this starts in a place, an area east of the Bastille, called the Faux-Bourg, that means neighborhood Saint-Antoine, Saint-Anthony.
sentences.zh: 所以这始于巴士底狱以东的一个地方，一个叫做圣安托万郊区（Faux-Bourg）的街区。

sentences.en: And there's a rumor that goes around, there's a big wallpaper manufacturer in town called Réveillon,
sentences.zh: 当时流传着一个谣言，城里有一个大型壁纸制造商叫雷韦永（Réveillon），

sentences.en: and there's a rumor that Réveillon had gone to a public meeting and had said that his workers should live on 15 sous a day, which is now the price of a loaf of bread,
sentences.zh: 有传言称雷韦永曾在一个公开会议上说，他的工人们每天靠15苏（sous）生活就够了，而这现在正是一个面包的价格，

sentences.en: one loaf only.
sentences.zh: 仅仅一个面包。

sentences.en: And actually, he hadn't said that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他根本没说过这话。

sentences.en: What he had said was that if they sorted out the economy and liberalized the economy, there would be lower prices, and then with lower prices, there would be lower wages,
sentences.zh: 他当时说的是，如果他们理顺经济并实现经济自由化，物价就会下降，随着物价下降，工资也会随之降低，

sentences.en: and one day his workers would live on 15 sous a day because bread would be so cheap, or words to that effect.
sentences.zh: 总有一天他的工人每天靠15苏就能生活，因为面包会变得非常便宜，或者大致是这个意思的话。

sentences.en: Now, Réveillon is very well known in Paris.
sentences.zh: 如今，雷韦永在巴黎可以说是大名鼎鼎。

sentences.en: He had made, in his capacity as a paper manufacturer, Tom, he had made the paper that was the first balloon, the Montgolfier balloon,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，作为一名造纸商，他曾制造过第一只热气球——也就是蒙戈尔费耶兄弟热气球所需的纸张，

sentences.en: and he had sponsored the first hot air balloons, and they had taken off from the yard of his workshop.
sentences.zh: 他还资助了第一批热气球，它们是从他作坊的院子里升空的。

sentences.en: So, you know, you will see his name if you Google the first hot air balloon flights.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，如果你用谷歌搜索第一批热气球飞行，你就会看到他的名字。

sentences.en: He is like a really modern, interesting person.
sentences.zh: 他就像是一个非常现代、有趣的人物。

sentences.en: He's kind of a James Dyson figure.
sentences.zh: 他有点像詹姆斯·戴森式的人物。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: Entrepreneur, technology.
sentences.zh: 企业家，代表着科技。

sentences.en: He's a really impressive person, this guy, Réveillon.
sentences.zh: 这家伙真的是个相当了不起的人，这个雷韦永。

sentences.en: He had been an apprentice paper worker.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名造纸学徒工。

sentences.en: He'd worked his way up.
sentences.zh: 他通过自己的努力一步步干了上来。

sentences.en: He'd bought his own paper workshop.
sentences.zh: 他买下了自己的造纸作坊。

sentences.en: By the 1780s, he's employing hundreds of workers.
sentences.zh: 到了18世纪80年代，他已经雇用了数百名工人。

sentences.en: He's brilliant at making wallpaper and paper generally.
sentences.zh: 他在制造壁纸和普通纸张方面堪称天才。

sentences.en: He's so good, he exports it to England, which, of course, given that England is the sort of…
sentences.zh: 他手艺极佳，甚至将其出口到英国——当然，考虑到英国本身就是那种……

sentences.en: Yeah, Coles to Newcastle.
sentences.zh: 对，运煤到纽卡斯尔。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's Coles to Newcastle, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，这就叫运煤到纽卡斯尔，一点没错。

sentences.en: He's also a very paternalistic employer.
sentences.zh: 他也是一位非常有家长作风的老板。

sentences.en: He pays his workers well more than his competitors, and he even pays them over that winter.
sentences.zh: 他给工人们支付的薪水远高于竞争对手，甚至在那个冬天也照常发工资。

sentences.en: When it's so cold, they can't work.
sentences.zh: 天气冷得无法干活时，

sentences.en: He says, I'll sort you out.
sentences.zh: 他说，我会照顾你们的。

sentences.en: So, he's a saint, a saintly figure from the end of a Dickens novel.
sentences.zh: 所以，他是个圣人，一个狄更斯小说结局里才会出现的圣人般的人物。

sentences.en: A lovely man.
sentences.zh: 一个可爱的人。

sentences.en: Adopting orphans.
sentences.zh: 收养孤儿。

sentences.en: Mr. Cheerable or something.
sentences.zh: 就像切鲁布尔先生或者类似的人物。

sentences.en: Anyway, because he's a capitalist entrepreneur, basically everybody hates him because he represents a threat.
sentences.zh: 总之，因为他是个资本主义企业家，基本上所有人都恨他，因为他构成了威胁。

sentences.en: He represents threatening modernity, putting sort of craftspeople out of work, like his rivals out of work.
sentences.zh: 他代表着一种威胁性的现代性，让一些手艺人失业，就像让他的竞争对手失业一样。

sentences.en: And so, as this story spreads, people in the neighbourhood say, yeah, let's go and smash up Réveillon's workshop.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着这个故事的传开，街坊邻居们纷纷说道，走吧，咱们去砸了雷韦永的作坊。

sentences.en: The first day they tried to do this, some of the local sort of politicians managed to turn them away.
sentences.zh: 他们试图动手的头一天，当地的一些政客设法把他们劝退了。

sentences.en: But the second day, the 28th of April, the crowd is swelled by unemployed dockers and brewers and tanners and things.
sentences.zh: 但在第二天，即4月28日，人群被失业的码头工人、酿酒工人、制革工人等壮大了队伍。

sentences.en: And about 5,000 to 10,000 people turn up outside.
sentences.zh: 大约有5,000到10,000人聚集在外面。

sentences.en: And do you think this is partly like in the election episode that we did a few weeks back?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这有点像我们几周前做的选举那一集吗？

sentences.en: People, you know, they're told there's going to be a Barney.
sentences.zh: 人们，你知道的，听说要大闹一场，

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: To turn up in front of it.
sentences.zh: 于是就跑去围观。

sentences.en: Yeah, but that's the thing about people hearing there's going to be a Barney and turning up to see the fun of it or to join in is key to all riots and revolutions, I think.
sentences.zh: 对，但这就是人们听说要打群架然后跑去看热闹或跟着瞎起哄的关键所在，我认为这也是所有暴动和革命的共同点。

sentences.en: So all these people turn up and they basically, they lay siege to his house and his workshop.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些人蜂拥而至，基本上对他的宅邸和作坊发动了围攻。

sentences.en: He and his family managed to get away.
sentences.zh: 他和他的家人设法逃了出去。

sentences.en: A force of nature, pagan, dangerous and uncontainable within clothes or custom.

sentences.zh: 他既写这种色情文学，也写非常恶毒的政治论战文章。

sentences.en: from the rest of the nobility.

sentences.en: The thing is that despite his appearance, he's basically a huge man when he's got this terrible skin and he's shouting about vampires and stuff.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，尽管他外表看起来如此——当他顶着这张可怕的皮肤，大喊着吸血鬼之类的话时，他其实是个身材魁梧的大汉。

sentences.en: But actually, behind all that, he's quite moderate.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，在这背後，他相当温和。

sentences.zh: 他想要英国那种体制的宪法。

sentences.zh: 他完全想要英国式的宪法。

sentences.en: And that's very sensible and reflects well on him.
sentences.zh: 这非常明智，也为他赢得了不少好感。

sentences.en: But he's determined to be seen as the supreme champion of the people in this whole imbroglio.
sentences.zh: 但他决心在这场混乱中把自己塑造成人民的至高无上的捍卫者。

sentences.zh: 所以，当他们举行游行时，他走路的姿态很奇特，把头向后仰，好让所有人都能看到他那颗巨大的脑袋，并且以一种略带

sentences.zh: 所以，他就像哈里·马奎尔。

sentences.zh: 对，他顶着一颗哈里·马奎尔的头。

sentences.zh: 如果你不知道哈里·马奎尔是谁的话……

sentences.zh: 哈里·马奎尔和火山的结合体。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 所以，大家对足球隐喻很感兴趣。

sentences.zh: 我弟弟曾经形容足球评论员马丁·基翁长得像困在流星里的鱼。

sentences.en: And that is Mirabeau's face.
sentences.zh: 这就是米拉波的脸。

sentences.en: A couple of other good characters from the third estate.
sentences.zh: 还有第三等级里另外几个不错的角色。

sentences.en: You've got Cies, the abbé who wrote What's the Third Estate?
sentences.zh: 你瞧，有西哀耶斯，那个写了《什么是第三等级？》的神甫。

sentences.en: There's our friend from Grenoble, Mr. Meunier, the first revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 还有我们来自格勒诺布尔的朋友穆尼埃先生，第一位革命家。

sentences.en: Yeah, the young judge.
sentences.zh: 对，年轻的法官。

sentences.zh: 还有一个来自阿拉斯的不为人知的年轻律师，名叫马克西米利安·克罗贝斯庇尔。

sentences.zh: 所以，他是米拉波的对照面。

sentences.en: Yeah, thin.
sentences.zh: 对，瘦。

sentences.zh: 苍白。

sentences.zh: 他是你。

sentences.zh: 米拉波是你。

sentences.zh: 我宁愿当米拉波。

sentences.zh: 对，你宁愿当米拉波也不愿当罗伯斯庇尔。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我的外形注定了我只能扮演罗伯斯庇尔，真是太惨了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 在他们这600人中，180人是律师，220人是法官或治安法官。

sentences.zh: 换句话说，这些第三等级的人，也就是所谓的平民，并不是法国的普通大众。

sentences.en: They are upwardly mobile winners.
sentences.zh: 他们是向上流动的成功人士。

sentences.en: People who actually are not very representative of the mass of the French people, but people who are incredibly articulate and ambitious.
sentences.zh: 这些人其实并不能代表法国大众的利益，但他们极具雄辩能力和野心。

sentences.en: And resentful of those above them.
sentences.zh: 并且对他们头顶上的人充满怨恨。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the trouble is that those above them don't make any effort to hide that they're above them or to include them.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，他们头顶上的人根本不屑于掩饰自己的高人一等，也不屑于接纳他们。

sentences.en: Well, isn't that the whole point of the Ancien Regime?
sentences.zh: 这不正是旧制度的核心所在吗？

sentences.en: It's all about hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 一切都是为了等级森严。

sentences.en: Of course it is.
sentences.zh: 当然是这样。

sentences.zh: 所以，那是5月4日的游行。

sentences.zh: 到了5月5日，他们在小娱乐厅开会，也就是凡尔赛的

sentences.en: Pleasures of Versailles.
sentences.zh: 小娱乐宫。

sentences.en: And Louis is on his throne.
sentences.zh: 国王坐在他的宝座上。

sentences.en: He's got Marie Antoinette to his side.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·安托瓦内特坐在他身旁。

sentences.en: There's a table for his ministers.
sentences.zh: 摆着一张给他大臣们坐的桌子。

sentences.en: Then you have the benches of the church and the nobility.
sentences.zh: 然后是教会和贵族的席位。

sentences.en: And then the third estate are all shoved down to the far end of the hall.
sentences.zh: 接着，第三等级全被挤到了大厅的最远端。

sentences.en: And the king gives a speech and he says, ah, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 国王发表了一番讲话，他说，啊，太棒了。

sentences.en: You're all here.
sentences.zh: 你们都来了。

sentences.en: I've been looking forward to this.
sentences.zh: 我一直盼望着这一天。

sentences.en: You know, everyone's great.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，大家都很好。

sentences.en: Should have done it before.
sentences.zh: 早就该这么做了。

sentences.zh: 他的确说过最近有很多关于革新的讨论。

sentences.en: I think this is much exaggerated.
sentences.zh: 我认为这大大被夸大了。

sentences.en: I don't want to hear any more of that.
sentences.zh: 我不想再听到这种言论了。

sentences.en: Then there's a strange business with his hat.
sentences.zh: 接着发生了一件关于他的帽子的诡异事情。

sentences.zh: 演讲结束时，他脱下了帽子。

sentences.en: And then the nobility doff their hats.
sentences.zh: 然后贵族们也脱下了他们的帽子。

sentences.en: Their beaver hats.
sentences.zh: 他们的海狸皮帽。

sentences.en: Their beaver hats.
sentences.zh: 他们的海狸皮帽。

sentences.en: Whatever.

sentences.zh: 因为尽管有一片混乱，随后却迎来了巨大的兴奋。

sentences.en: Of Jacques Necker giving a speech on fiscal policy and finance.
sentences.zh: 那就是雅克·内克发表关于财政政策和金融的演讲。

sentences.en: So, that must cheer them all up.
sentences.zh: 所以这一定能让大家振作起来。

sentences.en: Well, everyone's really looking forward to this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，每个人都非常期待这一刻。

sentences.zh: 然后所有人都开始昏昏欲睡。

sentences.en: People fall asleep.
sentences.zh: 人们纷纷睡着了。

sentences.en: Everybody says afterwards, oh my God, it's so disappointing.
sentences.zh: 事后每个人都说，天哪，太令人失望了。

sentences.zh: 当他们到达时，国王的人说，好了，你们要去各自的议事厅。

sentences.en: Formal and faintly chilly.
sentences.zh: 正式且略带冷意。
