sentences.zh: 因此他们把自己视为新罗马人。

sentences.en: But also there is an argument that it's been a great age the last 10, 20 years in France of the public theatre, popular theatre.
sentences.zh: 但也有观点认为，过去这十到二十年，法国迎来了公共戏剧和大众戏剧的伟大时代。

sentences.en: Well, we talked about how massively important the theatre is a couple of episodes ago with
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在前几集讨论《费加罗的婚礼》时就说过，戏剧是多么的重要。

sentences.en: The Marriage of Figaro.
sentences.zh: 费加罗的婚礼。

sentences.en: Yeah, The Marriage of Figaro is a perfect example because The Marriage of Figaro is very emotional, tear-stained, over-the-top, fun, you know, this sense of spectacle.
sentences.zh: 对，\u300a费加罗的婚礼\u300b就是一个完美的例子，因为\u300a费加罗的婚礼\u300b非常情绪化、满含泪水、夸张、有趣，你知道的，有一种奇观的感觉。

sentences.en: And for the first time, really, politics is deliberately emulating that.
sentences.zh: 而且这也是政治第一次真正地刻意去模仿这一点。

sentences.en: So there is a public gallery of the deliberations.
sentences.zh: 所以 deliberations 有了一个公众观景区。

sentences.en: The Third Estate are basically having a massive stalemate with the court and refusing to go ahead and be verified along with the other chambers.
sentences.zh: 第三等级基本上与王室陷入了巨大的僵局，拒绝继续前进并与其他等级一起接受验证。

sentences.en: And this stalemate continues.
sentences.zh: 而这个僵局还在继续。

sentences.en: And every day, you know, thousands of people will get coaches from Paris, come out to Versailles to watch the show.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，每天都有数千人坐着马车从巴黎来到凡尔赛看热闹。

sentences.en: The most famous one is an English traveller called Arthur Young, who is one of the great go-to sources on the early French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 最著名的是一个名叫亚瑟\u00b7扬的英国旅行者，他是研究法国大革命早期最重要的信息来源之一。

sentences.en: He's quoted in every single book.
sentences.zh: 他的话在每一本书里都被引用。

sentences.en: And he gets a coach out there.
sentences.zh: 他坐马车去了那里。

sentences.en: He has all the big names speaking.
sentences.zh: 所有的大人物都在发言。

sentences.en: He's excited about all the oratory.
sentences.zh: 他对所有的演讲都兴奋不已。

sentences.en: And he says what's shocking for him, coming from Britain, is that the spectators in the galleries clap and cheer and boo as though it is a play.
sentences.zh: 他说，作为一个英国人，对他来说最震撼的是，看台上的观众像看戏一样鼓掌、欢呼和倒彩。

sentences.en: And he says this is very bad.
sentences.zh: 他说这非常糟糕。

sentences.en: This is reducing politics to mere entertainment.
sentences.zh: 这把政治沦为了纯粹的娱乐。

sentences.en: But actually, this becomes central to the revolution.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这成为了大革命的核心。

sentences.en: Emotional outpourings.
sentences.zh: 情绪的宣泄。

sentences.en: And this idea of the orator, who is copying Roman models like Cicero, commanding people by the strength of his voice.
sentences.zh: 还有这种演说家的理念，他们模仿西塞罗等罗马楷模，用声音的力量来统领人们。

sentences.en: So Mirabe had a really good voice, perhaps bursting into tears while he's talking, which people think is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以米拉波的声音真的很好，说话时甚至可能会突然哭起来，人们觉得这太棒了。

sentences.en: But also, presumably, it's because unlike in Britain, where you have the House of Commons, you have the House of Lords, and you have elections where people go on the hustings.
sentences.zh: 但大概也是因为，与英国不同，英国有下议院，有上议院，还有人们参加竞选活动的选举。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so the traditions of political engagement are organic.
sentences.zh: 因此，政治参与的传统是有机的。

sentences.en: They've evolved.
sentences.zh: 它们是演变而来的。

sentences.en: They're not suddenly being portrayed to people as something new.
sentences.zh: 它们不是突然作为某种新事物展现在人们面前的。

sentences.en: In this occasion, no one's seen anything like this.
sentences.zh: 在这次活动中，谁也没见过这样的场面。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: They don't have regular elections.
sentences.zh: 他们没有定期选举。

sentences.en: They don't have the throwing of dead cats and the attacks with halberds that are such an important part of the British constitution.
sentences.zh: 他们没有扔死猫和用长戟袭击这些构成英国宪法重要部分的环节。

sentences.en: And so there must be a feeling that Mirabeau and everybody else is kind of feeling their way into roles that have not yet been defined.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们一定会觉得，米拉波和其他所有人都在摸索着进入尚未定义的角色。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Making it up.
sentences.zh: 现场现编。

sentences.en: What is politics?
sentences.zh: 什么是政治？

sentences.en: And what is the style of politics?
sentences.zh: 政治的风格又是什么？

sentences.en: What is the style of politics?
sentences.zh: 政治的风格是什么？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And they're drawing their style of politics from the theatre,
sentences.zh: 他们的政治风格取自戏剧，

sentences.en: from literature, from the kind of cultural mood of the time.
sentences.zh: 取自文学，取自当时的某种文化氛围。

sentences.en: And so this is clearly very much true of the members of the Third Estate, that they are playing a role simply by not moving, by sticking to their guns.
sentences.zh: 所以这在第三等级的成员身上显然非常明显，他们仅仅通过一动不动、坚持到底，就在扮演一个角色。

sentences.en: What about the First and Second Estates?
sentences.zh: 那第一和第二等级呢？

sentences.en: They must be watching this performance as well and thinking, maybe we should join it.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定也一直在看这场表演，并心想，也许我们也该加入进去。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Eventually.
sentences.zh: 最终会加入的。

sentences.en: They don't join straight away, though.
sentences.zh: 不过他们不会马上加入。

sentences.en: There's about a month before the first dribs and drabs from them come to join the Third
sentences.zh: 在大约一个月的时间里，才会陆续有零星的人加入第三

sentences.en: Estate.
sentences.zh: 等级。

sentences.en: So the stalemate is quite long lasting.
sentences.zh: 所以僵局持续了相当长的时间。

sentences.en: And in all that time, the stalemate is being reported back in Paris.
sentences.zh: 在整个这段时间里，僵局的消息一直被传回巴黎。

sentences.en: So Mirabeau, for example, his mistress owns a print shop, which is very convenient for him because he writes letters to his constituents telling them what's going on.
sentences.zh: 比如米拉波的情妇拥有一家印刷厂，这对他非常有利，因为他给选民写信告诉他们发生了什么。

sentences.en: And they go to the printers and they're released in Paris before they even get back to
sentences.zh: 这些信件送到印刷厂，甚至在它们运回

sentences.en: Aix-en-Provence.
sentences.zh: 艾克斯普罗旺斯之前，就已经在巴黎发布了。

sentences.en: So there's this stream of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以有这样源源不断的信息流。

sentences.en: So actually, it's not just a theatrical event.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这不仅仅是一场戏剧活动。

sentences.en: It's also a media event.
sentences.zh: 它也是一场媒体活动。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: The first mediated, mediatized political event of its kind.
sentences.zh: 这是同类中第一个被媒体报道、媒介化的政治事件。

sentences.en: Because there's this whole thing, isn't there, that Robert Darnton mentions about how people wear buttons with images of top political actors and things.
sentences.zh: 因为有这样一个现象，不是吗？罗伯特\u00b7达顿提到过，人们佩戴印有主要政治人物头像等图案的徽章。

sentences.en: So there is a sense in which the relationship of the people to the theatre can be mapped onto their relationship to what is going on in Versailles.
sentences.zh: 因此，某种程度上，人民与戏剧的关系可以映射到他们与凡尔赛正在发生的事情的关系上。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's definitely true.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这绝对是真的。

sentences.en: There is a sense that it's an entertainment, it's a spectacle, it's a sport, it's a fashion.
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，它是一种娱乐、一种奇观、一项运动、一种时尚。

sentences.en: And of course, it's of pressing importance because of the catastrophic state that people are in across the country and in Paris as well.
sentences.zh: 当然，它也具有紧迫的重要性，因为全国各地以及巴黎的人们都处于灾难性的状态中。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: So by the end of May, early June, there are really, really bleak apocalyptic reports coming in from the countryside.
sentences.zh: 所以在五月底、六月初，从乡间传来了非常非常黯淡的世界末日般的报告。

sentences.en: There are posters going up in Paris saying that if nothing changes, there's going to be an insurrection.
sentences.zh: 巴黎贴出了海报，上面写着如果什么都不改变，将会发生暴动。

sentences.en: You can imagine the scene calling for an uprising, those kind of posters.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象那个呼吁起义的场景，诸如此类的海报。

sentences.en: And that lends an urgency to all this.
sentences.zh: 这给这一切增添了一种紧迫感。

sentences.en: So on the 10th of June, the Abbé Siez says, look, we cannot wait any longer.
sentences.zh: 所以在6月10日，西哀士神父说，听着，我们不能再等了。

sentences.en: The court seemed determined to not let us sit with the other estates.
sentences.zh: 王室似乎决心不让我们与其他等级坐在一起。

sentences.en: Here's what we do.
sentences.zh: 我们这么做。

sentences.en: We will give them an ultimatum.
sentences.zh: 我们要给他们下最后通牒。

sentences.en: You come and sit with us.
sentences.zh: 你们来和我们坐在一起。

sentences.en: And whether they do or not, we will declare ourselves the National Assembly.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是否照做，我们都将宣布成立国民议会。

sentences.en: We will be the sole representatives of the nation.
sentences.zh: 我们将成为国家的唯一代表。

sentences.en: And we will take the nation's fate into our hands.
sentences.zh: 我们将把国家的命运掌握在自己手中。

sentences.en: I mean, this is an unbelievable thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太让人难以置信了。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: They're in Versailles.
sentences.zh: 他们身处凡尔赛。

sentences.en: The monarch is only hundreds of yards away in some other room.
sentences.zh: 君主就在几百码外的另一个房间里。

sentences.en: And they're basically saying, we will take this into our own hands.
sentences.zh: 而他们基本上是在说，我们要把命运掌握在自己手中。

sentences.en: But also, they're laying claim to the sovereignty that traditionally has been that of the monarch.
sentences.zh: 但同时，他们也在宣称拥有传统上属于君主的最高权力。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, I mean, at this point, I don't think they recognise that, do they?
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，此时此刻，我觉得他们并没有意识到这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I think they still think this is kind of going to be a rerun of Britain's Glorious Revolution.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想他们仍然认为这有点像是英国光荣革命的重演。

sentences.en: And it won't go too far.
sentences.zh: 而且不会发展得太远。

sentences.en: Eventually, Louis will give in and it'll be all fine.
sentences.zh: 最终路易会妥协，一切都会好的。

sentences.en: I think a lot of them still do think that.
sentences.zh: 我想他们中的很多人仍然是这么想的。

sentences.en: And you asked, Tom, and I didn't answer it properly, for which I apologise to you, hand on heart, about the first two estates.
sentences.zh: 你刚才问我，汤姆，而我没有好好回答，对此我向你致以由衷的歉意，关于前两个等级的情况。

sentences.en: Some of them are now beginning to come across.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人现在开始倒戈了。

sentences.en: So on the 13th of June, there was a real breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 所以在6月13日，出现了一个真正的突破。

sentences.en: Some parish priests come across.
sentences.zh: 一些教区神父过来了。

sentences.en: And actually, the first estate, the clergy, they are actually the ones who are closest to the mass of ordinary French men and women.
sentences.zh: 实际上，第一等级，也就是神职人员，他们其实是与广大普通法国民众最亲近的人。

sentences.en: Because most of the clergy's deputies are not archbishops with kind of sumptuous Cardinal Wolsey-style robes.
sentences.zh: 因为大多数神职人员代表并不是穿着华丽的沃尔西红衣主教式长袍的大主教。

sentences.en: They're ordinary parish priests.
sentences.zh: 他们是普通的教区神父。

sentences.en: Who are often very poor themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们自己往往也很穷。

sentences.en: Very poor.
sentences.zh: 非常穷。

sentences.en: And who actually understand the peasants better than some of the third estate lawyers do.
sentences.zh: 而且他们实际上比某些第三等级的律师更懂农民。

sentences.en: So more and more of these priests come over in the next few days, rising to about 100 of the priests.
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的几天里，越来越多的神父加入过来，大约增加到了100名神父。

sentences.en: And on the 17th of June, they say, enough, time has run out.
sentences.zh: 而在6月17日，他们说，够了，时间到了。

sentences.en: We are going to now call ourselves, as it were, a National Assembly.
sentences.zh: 我们现在要自称为国民议会。

sentences.en: The amusing thing is they can't decide what the name should be.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他们无法决定应该叫什么名字。

sentences.en: So Sies says, our title, which will resound down the generations, is the Known and Verifiable Representatives.
sentences.zh: 于是西哀士说，我们的称号，将名扬后世，那就是“已知且可验证的代表”。

sentences.en: So this is very like us trying to decide what to call episodes of our podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这非常像我们试图决定给我们的播客单集起什么名字。

sentences.en: It's actually like you wanting the podcast to be called PodpaSt.
sentences.zh: 其实就像你希望这个播客叫 PodpaSt 一样。

sentences.en: I still regret that.
sentences.zh: 我到现在还很后悔。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You're about to stick with that.
sentences.zh: 你差不多要坚持用这个名字了。

sentences.en: And this is the first time I've ever heard you say that you regret it.
sentences.zh: 这也是我第一次听到你说你后悔。

sentences.en: I just think it would have been a very good name, but whatever.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得那会是个很好的名字，但随它去吧。

sentences.en: Oh, sorry.
sentences.zh: 哦，抱歉。

sentences.en: You don't regret having come up with it?
sentences.zh: 你难道不后悔自己想出这个名字吗？

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，一点也不。

sentences.en: No, I'm very proud of it.
sentences.zh: 不，我为此感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: Well, so Emounier, the guy from Grenoble, he says, that's a terrible name.
sentences.zh: 好吧，穆尼埃，那个来自格勒诺布尔的家伙，他说，这名字太糟糕了。

sentences.en: The known Verifiable Representatives.
sentences.zh: “已知可验证的代表”。

sentences.en: He says, I've got a very catchy name.
sentences.zh: 他说，我有一个非常朗朗上口的名字。

sentences.en: He's the Tom Holland of the third estate.
sentences.zh: 他就是第三等级的汤姆\u00b7霍兰德。

sentences.en: He's still got a brilliant name.
sentences.zh: 他还是想出了一个绝妙的名字。

sentences.en: I think we should be called the legitimate assembly, the representatives of the larger part of the nation acting in the absence of the smaller part.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们应该被称为合法议会，即在少数人缺席的情况下代表国家大部分人的代表。

sentences.en: No, I'm about compression, PodpaSt.
sentences.zh: 不，我喜欢精简，PodpaSt。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样。

sentences.en: Anyway, listen, let's not get into that.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，听着，我们别讨论这个了。

sentences.en: So they have a succession of terrible names.
sentences.zh: 所以他们接连想出了一堆糟糕的名字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But eventually they decide, let's go for National Assembly.
sentences.zh: 但最终他们决定，就叫国民议会吧。

sentences.en: Let's cut to the chase.
sentences.zh: 咱们开门见山吧。

sentences.en: They eventually said, let's just call it the National Assembly.
sentences.zh: 他们最终说，就叫它国民议会吧。

sentences.en: Now, there's a sense, I think, at this point of them self-radicalizing, anything being possible.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为在这个时候，他们有一种自我激进化的感觉，一切皆有可能。

sentences.en: They say that basically all existing taxation is illegal because they haven't authorized it.
sentences.zh: 他们说，基本上所有现存的税收都是非法的，因为他们没有批准过。

sentences.en: But for the time being, they're happy to let the existing taxes continue until they have drawn up the new, remember, they, not the king, have drawn up the new tax system.
sentences.zh: 但目前，他们乐意让现有的税收继续下去，直到他们制定出新的税收制度——记住，是他们，而不是国王，制定了新的税收制度。

sentences.en: So this is, as you said, I mean, they're seizing sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，我的意思是，他们在夺取最高权力。

sentences.en: It is really an incredible thing.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一件不可思议的事情。

sentences.en: Louis is very, very deeply depressed during all this.
sentences.zh: 在这期间，路易感到非常非常深度的沮丧。

sentences.en: I mean, he's got, as you said, Tom, quite large, he's eating a lot, he's messing around with his locks.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如你所说，汤姆，他体型相当胖，吃得很多，还摆弄着他的锁。

sentences.en: He feels very sad that this is spiraling out of control.
sentences.zh: 他感到非常难过，因为这一切正在失控。

sentences.en: And then a terrible thing happens, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 然后可怕的事情发生了，对吧？

sentences.en: The Dofa, his son, his much-loved son, dies.
sentences.zh: 王太子，他的儿子，他深爱的儿子，去世了。

sentences.en: On the 4th of June, dies of TB and actually dies, we won't go into all the details because
sentences.zh: 在6月4日，死于结核病，而且实际上——我们不会细说所有细节，因为

sentences.en: I think it actually is unnecessary and horrible, but this little boy dies a very agonizing, lingering death from TB.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这既没必要又很可怕，但这个小男孩因结核病经历了非常痛苦、漫长的死亡。

sentences.en: He's just seven years old.
sentences.zh: 他才七岁。

sentences.en: And Louis and Marie Antoinette are understandably, absolutely distraught.
sentences.zh: 路易和玛丽\u00b7安托瓦内特可想而知，完全崩溃了。

sentences.en: And in a weird way, actually, I think almost all the history books, even the best ones, underplay this.
sentences.zh: 而且从某种诡异的角度来看，实际上，我认为几乎所有的历史书，甚至是最好的那些，都低估了这一点。

sentences.en: They just say, oh, by the way, his son died and he's very upset and he withdraws.
sentences.zh: 他们只是说，哦，顺便说一句，他的儿子死了，他很难过，然后他退居幕后了。

sentences.en: But I mean, this for him is a loss of unbelievable proportions, just horrendous.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，这对他的打击是难以想象的巨大，简直太可怕了。

sentences.en: Because unusually, for a French king, he hasn't had a mistress.
sentences.zh: 因为不同寻常的是，作为法国国王，他没有情妇。

sentences.en: He's very much a family man.
sentences.zh: 他非常顾家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Marie Antoinette as well is a very good mother.
sentences.zh: 而且玛丽\u00b7安托瓦内特也是个好母亲。

sentences.en: So they are engaged with their children in a way that is unusual, but reflects the kind of sentimental ideas of Rousseau.
sentences.zh: 所以他们与孩子的互动方式很不寻常，但这反映了卢梭的那种感伤主义思想。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So he withdraws from public business.
sentences.zh: 于是他从公众事务中退居幕后。

sentences.en: He leaves, he physically leaves Versailles for his country estate at Mali, Mali Leroy.
sentences.zh: 他离开了，他肉体上离开了凡尔赛，前往他在马利（马利勒鲁瓦）的乡村庄园。

sentences.en: And there he is lost in mourning.
sentences.zh: 而他就这样陷入了哀悼之中。

sentences.en: So he's not taking charge of all this.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有掌控这一切。

sentences.en: It's spiraling out of control.
sentences.zh: 局势正在失控。

sentences.en: When he finally rouses himself and comes back to Versailles, he has a big meeting with
sentences.zh: 当他终于振作起来回到凡尔赛时，他与

sentences.en: Necker and with his brothers, who are much more hardline than he is, and with the queen.
sentences.zh: 内克尔、态度比他强硬得多的兄弟们以及王后举行了一场重要会议。

sentences.en: What on earth are we going to do?
sentences.zh: 我们到底该怎么办？

sentences.en: And Necker says, I think we should probably give in to the third estate at this point.
sentences.zh: 内克尔说，我想我们此时或许应该向第三等级妥协。

sentences.en: We've got to meet them halfway.
sentences.zh: 我们必须做出退让，与他们会面。

sentences.en: And Marie Antoinette and his brothers say, this business has got massively out of control.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·安托瓦内特和他的兄弟们说，事情已经彻底失控了。

sentences.en: It's Necker's fault.
sentences.zh: 这是内克尔的错。

sentences.en: We should shut all this down now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在应该把这一切都叫停。

sentences.en: And Louis can't decide.
sentences.zh: 而路易却拿不定主意。

sentences.en: So what he does is a typical Louis thing of a bit of change, but not too much, which doesn't satisfy anybody.
sentences.zh: 所以他采取了典型的路易式做法：做出一点改变，但又不多，结果谁也没能讨好。

sentences.en: He says, I'll bring all the estates together in what he calls a séance royale, a grand meeting.
sentences.zh: 他说，我将把各等级召集在一起，召开他所谓的“国王御前会议”（séance royale），一场盛大的会议。

sentences.en: And I'll offer them some reforms, but they have to abandon all this rubbish and tosh about a national assembly.
sentences.zh: 我会向他们提供一些改革，但他们必须放弃关于国民议会的那些垃圾和废话。

sentences.en: Like, this is no good.
sentences.zh: 就像是在说，这根本行不通。

sentences.en: So I want to have this big meeting and they're going to have it in the hall where the third estate had been meeting and they have to set it up.
sentences.zh: 所以我想要召开这场大集会，他们将在第三等级开会的那个大厅里开会，而且他们必须布置好会场。

sentences.en: They literally have to set up the room.
sentences.zh: 他们真的得亲自动手布置房间。

sentences.en: On the morning of the 20th of June, his workmen go in to build the platforms necessary for this meeting where he is going to lay down the law.
sentences.zh: 6月20日清晨，他的工人们进去搭建平台，以便召开这场由他来独裁专断的会议。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, they put up signs outside saying, you know, the third estate can't meet here today.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们在外面挂出了告示，你知道的，说明第三等级今天不能在这里开会。

sentences.en: The third estate all arrive to find the doors are closed and there are guards blocking the way and there are signs coming up about a big meeting with the king.
sentences.zh: 第三等级的人陆续赶到，却发现大门紧闭，有卫兵挡住去路，还贴出了关于国王要召开大会的告示。

sentences.en: And there are hundreds of armed guards standing around blocking their way.
sentences.zh: 周围站着几百名手持武器的卫兵，挡住了他们的去路。

sentences.en: And it is also pouring with rain.
sentences.zh: 而且当时还下着倾盆大雨。

sentences.en: So they're all getting soaked and they expected to go into the hall and have their meeting.
sentences.zh: 所以大家都被淋得湿透，而他们原本以为能走进大厅开会的。

sentences.en: What are they going to do?
sentences.zh: 他们该怎么办？

sentences.en: And lots of them say, well, I'm not just going to go home to bed.
sentences.zh: 许多人说，好吧，我可不会直接回家睡觉。

sentences.en: We should have our meeting on our own as the National Assembly, as normal.
sentences.zh: 我们应该像往常一样，作为国民议会独立召开我们的会议。

sentences.en: And one of them, a man called Dr. Geek.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人，一个名叫吉约丹医生的人。

sentences.en: Tom, you love this.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你最喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: Well, I love the way that much loved characters and indeed implements of execution are kind of subtly introduced in unexpected angled ways.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我喜欢这种方式，那些深受喜爱的角色，甚至是处决工具，竟然以这种出人意料的巧妙方式被引入进来。

sentences.en: So what's the name of this doctor?
sentences.zh: 那这位医生的名字叫什么？

sentences.en: Dr. Guillotin, who is mindful of interesting devices, Tom, rational devices for law and order.
sentences.zh: 吉约丹医生，他很关心那些有趣的装置，汤姆，为了法律和秩序的理性装置。

sentences.en: Dr. Guillotin says, oh, a friend of mine owns a tennis court around the corner.
sentences.zh: 吉约丹医生说，哦，我的一个朋友在拐角处开了一个网球场。

sentences.en: We could go and meet there.
sentences.zh: 我们可以去那里开会。

sentences.en: It's in the rue du Vieux Versailles, the old Versailles street.
sentences.zh: 它在旧凡尔赛街（rue du Vieux Versailles）上。

sentences.en: Now, often you read popular accounts and they say the royal tennis court at Versailles.
sentences.zh: 通常你读到大众通俗读物时，他们会说那是凡尔赛的皇家网球场。

sentences.en: Anyway, that's not right at all.
sentences.zh: 总之，这种说法完全不对。

sentences.en: The game that is being played is a game called real tennis, jeu de paume in French, but it's not the king's court or anything like it.
sentences.zh: 人们玩的那种游戏叫做实网球（real tennis，法语里叫 jeu de paume），但它根本不是国王的球场，也完全不是那么回事。

sentences.en: It's some friend of Dr. Guillotin's who owns the court.
sentences.zh: 那是吉约丹医生某个朋友拥有的球场。

sentences.en: Anyway, they all pile into this tennis court.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们全都涌进了这个网球场。

sentences.en: So a real tennis is a little bit like squash, but with a very hard ball.
sentences.zh: 实网球有点像壁球，但球非常硬。

sentences.en: So it's indoors.
sentences.zh: 所以它是在室内进行的。

sentences.en: It's kind of an echoey, very stark, like a squash court.
sentences.zh: 有点像回音阵阵、非常空旷的壁球场。

sentences.en: They're all soaked with the rain.
sentences.zh: 他们都被雨水淋透了。

sentences.en: They all pile into this place.
sentences.zh: 他们全都涌进了这个地方。

sentences.en: It's very plain, very drab, very stark.
sentences.zh: 这里非常简陋、单调、空旷。

sentences.en: But actually, that kind of suits them.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这倒挺合他们的心意。

sentences.en: It does, because it's classical, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 确实如此，因为这很古典，对吧？

sentences.en: Potentially.
sentences.zh: 潜在地说是这样的。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 的确如此。

sentences.en: And it gives them a perfect opportunity to swear an oath.
sentences.zh: 这给他们提供了一个宣誓的绝佳机会。

sentences.en: Yeah, because Mounier, the man from Grenoble, he says, what we should all do is we should now swear an oath.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为格勒诺布尔出身的穆尼耶说，我们现在都应该做的是，我们应该宣誓。

sentences.en: Now, they've all used to this because the big hit painting of the last few years was by David, who you'll be talking about in a subsequent later episode, won't you, one day?
sentences.zh: 现在，他们对这种形式都很熟悉了，因为过去几年最轰动的画作是达维德画的，你以后会在后面的某集节目里聊到他，对吧，总有一天？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: When we finally get around to finishing this huge French Revolution epic.
sentences.zh: 当我们终于腾出时间拍完这部宏大的法国大革命史诗时。

sentences.en: David had done a painting called The Oath of the Horatii, hadn't he?
sentences.zh: 达维德曾画过一幅名为《贺拉斯兄弟的宣誓》的画，对吧？

sentences.en: About three brothers who sacrificed themselves for Rome, or offered to sacrifice themselves for Rome.
sentences.zh: 讲的是三个为了罗马而牺牲自己，或者主动提出为罗马牺牲自己的兄弟。

sentences.en: So martyrs, patriots.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是烈士，是爱国者。

sentences.en: And they all decide they want to copy this painting.
sentences.zh: 于是他们都决定模仿这幅画。

sentences.en: So they swear an oath to God and the patrie, the fatherland.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们向上帝和祖国（la patrie）宣誓。

sentences.en: They will never separate until they've written a new constitution for France.
sentences.zh: 在为法国写出新宪法之前，他们绝不分离。

sentences.en: And they say, listen, we don't even need a palace or a courtroom because we are the National
sentences.zh: 他们说，听着，我们甚至不需要宫殿或法庭，因为我们就是国民议会

sentences.en: Assembly and the National Assembly will exist wherever we come together.
sentences.zh: 而国民议会将在我们聚首的任何地方存在。

sentences.en: And then they raise their arms, as in David's painting.
sentences.zh: 然后他们举起手臂，就像达维德画中的那样。

sentences.en: They stretch out their right arms, not often, not a brilliant look, to be fair, tainted by subsequent misconduct in the 20th century, but that's by the by.
sentences.zh: 他们伸出右臂——说实话，这姿势不太常见，看起来也不算绝佳，因为后来在20世纪被一些不当行为玷污了，但那是题外话。

sentences.en: They stretch out their right arms, they put the other hand on their heart, and they swear this oath.
sentences.zh: 他们伸出右臂，把另一只手放在心口，庄严宣誓。

sentences.en: A great act of theatre, again, classic act of theatre, inspired by a painting, the media, by paintings, by paintings and the subsequent engravings that reproduce the painting.
sentences.zh: 这又是一场伟大的戏剧表演，经典的戏剧表演，灵感来自于绘画、媒体、绘画以及复制这幅画的后世版画。

sentences.en: There's incredible kind of meta self-consciousness about the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 整件事情带有一种令人难以置信的元自我意识。

sentences.en: There is, exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，一点没错。

sentences.en: Everybody's, well, it's, what do they call it?
sentences.zh: 每个人都在，嗯，这是，他们管这叫什么来着？

sentences.en: Cosplaying.
sentences.zh: Cosplay（角色扮演）。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's what they're doing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 他们就是在搞这个，对吧？

sentences.en: They're basically dressing up and pretending to be Romans.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是在盛装打扮，假装自己是罗马人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The news spreads very quickly.
sentences.zh: 消息传得极快。

sentences.en: They've sworn this oath in this tennis court.
sentences.zh: 他们在这个网球场里宣誓了。

sentences.en: There are printed copies of the oath on sale in Paris the next morning.
sentences.zh: 第二天早晨，印有誓言文本的印刷品就在巴黎公开出售了。

sentences.en: Louis' brothers and the other hardliners in the court go absolutely ballistic at this.
sentences.zh: 路易的兄弟们和宫廷里的其他强硬派对此气急败坏。

sentences.en: I love their solution to the whole problem.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢他们解决整个问题的方法了。

sentences.en: The comte d'artois, he just says, brilliant, I'll just go and book the tennis court.
sentences.zh: 阿图瓦伯爵（comte d'artois）直接说，太棒了，我去把那个网球场预定下来。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他真的这么做了。

sentences.en: He books the tennis court to stop them.
sentences.zh: 他把网球场订下来以阻止他们。

sentences.en: It's really funny.
sentences.zh: 这真的太搞笑了。

sentences.en: What's in my mind that I haven't been able to resolve is, did he play tennis?
sentences.zh: 我脑子里一直有个没想通的问题是，他去打网球了吗？

sentences.en: Well, who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: I mean, once you've booked the court, you're mad not to use it, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，既然你已经订了场地，不用就太疯狂了吧？

sentences.en: What else are you going to be doing?
sentences.zh: 不然你还打算干嘛？

sentences.en: Especially if it's raining.
sentences.zh: 尤其是下雨天的时候。

sentences.en: Anyway, the 23rd of June, so three days later, is going to be this big séance royale, a big summit meeting where Louis is going to decide all this.
sentences.zh: 总之，6月23日，也就是三天后，将举行这场盛大的御前会议，这是一场大型峰会，路易将在会上对这一切做出裁决。

sentences.en: And again, crazily, I mean, such a failure of statecraft, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 同样荒谬的是，我的意思是，这真是治国方略的彻底失败。

sentences.en: He humiliates the third estate.
sentences.zh: 他羞辱了第三等级。

sentences.en: The church and the nobility are seated firSt.
sentences.zh: 教会和贵族首先入座。

sentences.en: The third estate have to wait outside in the rain for an hour, and then they're brought in through a side door.
sentences.zh: 第三等级则不得不顶着雨在外面等了一个小时，然后才被从侧门带进去。

sentences.en: When they get in, they find that Necker is not there.
sentences.zh: 等他们进去后，发现内克尔不在场。

sentences.en: It is clear that Necker has lost the argument within the regime, and he is refusing to come or has been told to stay away.
sentences.zh: 很明显，内克尔在政权内部的辩论中已经失势，他拒绝出席或者被告知不准出席。

sentences.en: And Louis speaks for just half an hour.
sentences.zh: 路易只讲了短短半小时。

sentences.en: He says, I'll give you some of what you want.
sentences.zh: 他说，我会满足你们的一部分诉求。

sentences.en: Taxes will now have to be approved by the nation's representatives, and I promise that the estates general will meet regularly.
sentences.zh: 税收今后必须得到国家代表的批准，我保证三级会议将定期召开。

sentences.en: But he says, this stuff about the National Assembly is gibberish and nonsense.
sentences.zh: 但他说，关于国民议会的这些言论纯属胡言乱语、一派胡言。

sentences.en: I will not accept it.
sentences.zh: 我绝不接受。

sentences.en: The distinction of the three orders of the state is not up for debate.
sentences.zh: 国家三个等级的区别不容争论。

sentences.en: The clergy and the nobility must run their own affairs, and they can't be run for them by the third estate.
sentences.zh: 神职人员和贵族必须自行处理事务，第三等级无权代为处理。

sentences.en: Because, of course, if the moderate position is to emulate the British Constitution, Britain does have that division, House of Lords and House of Commons.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，如果温和派的立场是效仿英国宪法的话，英国确实存在这种划分，即上议院和下议院。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not wholly reactionary in that sense.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从这个意义上说，它并不完全是反动的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's not wholly reactionary.
sentences.zh: 对，它并不完全反动。

sentences.en: I mean, they're going well beyond the British Constitution now, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们现在的行径已经远远超越了英国宪法，不是吗？

sentences.en: And they're going well beyond the American Constitution.
sentences.zh: 而且他们已经远远超越了美国宪法。

sentences.en: So they are doing away with the checks and balances that were so important for the United States, because they're all about the general will, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 因此，他们正在废除对美国至关重要的制衡机制，因为他们满脑子想的都是公意（general will），不是吗？

sentences.en: Which is not something that the founding fathers in America were so keen on.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是美国国父们那么热衷的东西。

sentences.en: Now, had Louis said all this two years earlier, maybe the whole story would be different.
sentences.zh: 如果在两年前路易就说出这些话，也许整个故事就会完全不同了。

sentences.en: But he didn't.
sentences.zh: 但他没有。

sentences.en: And it's too late, because, as we said, they've self-radicalized.
sentences.zh: 现在已经太迟了，因为正如我们所说，他们已经自我激化了。

sentences.en: So when he gets up and goes out after half an hour, everybody else starts to file out.
sentences.zh: 所以当他在半小时后起身离去时，其他所有人都开始鱼贯而出。

sentences.en: And the workmen come back in to demolish the platform.
sentences.zh: 工人们又回来拆除讲台。

sentences.en: And the third estate do not move.
sentences.zh: 而第三等级纹丝不动。

sentences.en: They're sitting there.
sentences.zh: 他们就坐在那里。

sentences.en: They will not move.
sentences.zh: 他们绝不离开。

sentences.en: This is their hall, and they're not going to budge.
sentences.zh: 这是他们的大厅，他们绝不挪窝。

sentences.en: And the Marquis de Treux-Breset.
sentences.zh: 还有德·布雷泽侯爵（Marquis de Treux-Breset）。

sentences.en: He's the suit guy.
sentences.zh: 他就是那个讲究着装的人。

sentences.en: The suits man.
sentences.zh: 正装男。

sentences.en: The correct thing you wear.
sentences.zh: 穿得合乎规矩的人。

sentences.en: Derek Guy.
sentences.zh: 德里克·盖伊（Derek Guy）。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's him.
sentences.zh: 对，就是他。

sentences.en: He says to them, you've got to go.
sentences.zh: 他对他们说，你们必须离开。

sentences.en: Right, we're trying to clear the room.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们要清场了。

sentences.en: You've got to go.
sentences.zh: 你们必须得走了。

sentences.en: And Mirabeau, by his own account, which is maybe a little bit self-dramatizing, says,
sentences.zh: 而米拉波根据他自己的叙述——可能有点自我戏剧化色彩——说道：

sentences.en: Go and tell those who have sent you that we are here by the will of the people, and we will only be driven out at the points of bayonets.
sentences.zh: 去告诉那些派你来的人，我们是奉人民的意志来到这里的，只有刺刀才能把我们逼退。

sentences.en: Very impressive stuff.
sentences.zh: 非常震撼的话。

sentences.en: And the Marquis, he retreats, because he's such a stickler for protocol.
sentences.zh: 侯爵退下了，因为他是个墨守成规的教条主义者。

sentences.en: He retreats, walking slowly backwards.
sentences.zh: 他一边退，一边慢吞吞地往后走。

sentences.en: It's a very strange image.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常奇怪的画面。

sentences.en: This man with the face like a crater has given this speech to him.
sentences.zh: 这个长着一张满是坑洼的脸的男人竟然对他说出了这番话。

sentences.en: Well, etiquette is etiquette, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，礼节就是礼节，对吧？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And then Louis, poor Louis, he's just not a hard man.
sentences.zh: 然后路易，可怜的路易，他就是不够狠。

sentences.en: He's not ruthless.
sentences.zh: 他不够冷酷。

sentences.en: Because when the Marquis tells Louis this, Louis just says, oh, well, let them stay.
sentences.zh: 因为当侯爵把这番话告诉路易时，路易只是说，哦，那就让他们留着吧。

sentences.en: If they want to stay, let them stay.
sentences.zh: 如果他们想留下，就让他们留下好了。

sentences.en: Fair dues.
sentences.zh: 算了吧。

sentences.en: So it's a classic Louis.
sentences.zh: 所以这很符合路易的风格。

sentences.en: He sort of parades his authority, but then he never, ever enforces it.
sentences.zh: 他有点像是在炫耀自己的权威，但却从不真正去执行它。

sentences.en: He always gives him.
sentences.zh: 他总是妥协。

sentences.en: So the next few days, more and more people join this National Assembly from the clergy and the nobility.
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的几天里，越来越多的神职人员和贵族加入了这个国民议会。

sentences.en: And then on 27th of June, only four days later, Louis does give in.
sentences.zh: 然后就在6月27日，仅仅四天后，路易真的妥协了。

sentences.en: His position has eroded.
sentences.zh: 他的地位已经被侵蚀殆尽。

sentences.en: It's a classic example of how in revolutionary situations, momentum is all.
sentences.zh: 这是革命局势中势头决定一切的又一个经典例证。

sentences.en: His position has eroded.
sentences.zh: 他的立场已经动摇了。

sentences.en: And he says, OK, yeah, I've changed my mind.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，好吧，行吧，我改变主意了。

sentences.en: I give up.
sentences.zh: 我放弃。

sentences.en: He orders the nobility and the clergy join the National Assembly now.
sentences.zh: 他下令让贵族和神职人员现在就加入国民议会。

sentences.en: You know, after all this, I've loSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，经历了这一切，我输了。

sentences.en: There is an explosion of joy in Versailles, a very, very revealing scene.
sentences.zh: 凡尔赛宫爆发了一阵喜悦，这是一个非常非常具有启示意义的场景。

sentences.en: So people are chanting.
sentences.zh: 所以人们在齐声高呼。

sentences.en: The crowds are in Versailles.
sentences.zh: 人群聚集在凡尔赛宫。

sentences.en: And they're shouting, Vive Necker, Vive le Roi.
sentences.zh: 他们在大喊：“内克尔万岁，国王万岁。”

sentences.en: And on the balcony of Louis XIV's bedroom, which overlooks the marble court of Versailles,
sentences.zh: 在俯瞰凡尔赛宫大理石庭院的《路易十四卧室》的阳台上，

sentences.en: Louis and Marie Antoinette come out onto the balcony and they pretend to look happy and to wave to the crowds who are shouting, long live the king.
sentences.zh: 路易和玛丽·安托瓦内特走到阳台上，他们假装看起来很高兴，向高呼国王万岁的人群挥手。

sentences.en: And actually, I always think it's a telling detail.
sentences.zh: 其实，我一直觉得这是一个很有说服力的细节。

sentences.en: People are very shocked at the appearance of Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 人们对玛丽·安托瓦内特的出现感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: Obviously, she's a grieving mother.
sentences.zh: 显然，她是一位正在悲痛中的母亲。

sentences.en: Yeah, she's grief stricken.
sentences.zh: 是的，她悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: And they say, lots of people said, she looks as though she's aged so much.
sentences.zh: 很多人都说，她看起来苍老了许多。

sentences.en: Her hair is grey.
sentences.zh: 她的头发都白了。

sentences.en: She's not wearing jewels.
sentences.zh: 她没有佩戴珠宝。

sentences.en: She looks terrible.
sentences.zh: 她看起来糟糕透了。

sentences.en: You know, it's understandable.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这也是可以理解的。

sentences.en: And she seems to be forcing back tears.
sentences.zh: 她似乎在强忍着泪水。

sentences.en: And she brings out her children, Marie Therese and Louis.
sentences.zh: 她带出了她的孩子，玛丽·特蕾丝和路易。

sentences.en: Marie Therese is 10 and Louis is 4.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·特蕾丝10岁，路易4岁。

sentences.en: And she brings them out, which the royal family have never done anything like this before.
sentences.zh: 她把他们带了出来，王室以前从来没有做过这样的事情。

sentences.en: And the crowd go mad.
sentences.zh: 人群陷入了疯狂。

sentences.en: They're cheering and all this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们在欢呼，还有诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: But I always think there's a sense, even here, that they have become prisoners of the crowd, that they're prisoners of the situation.
sentences.zh: 但我总觉得，即使在这里，也有一种感觉：他们已经成了人群的阶下囚，他们成了时局的囚徒。

sentences.en: They're parading.
sentences.zh: 他们在游行展示。

sentences.en: Yeah, they've lost agency.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们失去了自主权。

sentences.en: To appease the crowd.
sentences.zh: 为了安抚人群。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Now, some people think, in fact, lots of people think this is probably the end of the story now.
sentences.zh: 现在，有些人认为，实际上很多人认为，这可能就是这个故事的结局了。

sentences.en: The French Revolution has come and gone.
sentences.zh: 法国大革命已经过去。

sentences.en: So Arthur Young, the traveller that I mentioned, famously wrote in his journal or whatever it was, the whole business now seems over and the revolution complete.
sentences.zh: 正如我提到过的旅行家阿瑟·扬，他在日记或诸如此类的东西中写下了名言：整个事件现在似乎已经结束，革命已经完成。

sentences.en: But not everybody.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有人这么认为。

sentences.en: So that guy that we mentioned, the Marquis de Ferrière, the nobleman, the Enlightenment guy, he writes to his sister the next day.
sentences.zh: 正如我们提到的那个家伙，贵族、启蒙运动分子费里耶尔侯爵，他在第二天写信给他的姐姐。

sentences.en: And he says, we've come close to the bloodiest catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们已经接近了最血腥的灾难。

sentences.en: The weakness of the government seems to allow for anything.
sentences.zh: 政府的软弱似乎让一切都有可能发生。

sentences.en: People speak openly in the Palais Royale of massacring us.
sentences.zh: 人们在皇家宫殿公开谈论要屠杀我们。

sentences.en: Our houses are marked out for murder.
sentences.zh: 我们的房子已被标记为谋杀的目标。

sentences.en: He goes on to say, he says, everything may seem tranquil, but the troops are no longer obeying their officers.
sentences.zh: 他接着说，一切看起来可能很平静，但军队已经不再听从军官的指挥了。

sentences.en: He says, the Estates General of 1789 may be celebrated one day, he says, but it will be by a banner of blood that will be carried to all the parts of Europe.
sentences.zh: 他说，1789年的三部会议总有一天会被庆祝，但他指出，那将是一面带着血迹的旗帜，传遍欧洲各地。

sentences.en: So would it be fair to say, Dominic, that storm clouds really are gathering now?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，那么这样说是否公平：乌云现在确实正在聚集？

sentences.en: They are gathering because in the next few days, there are rumours that there are military units on the march out there in the provinces.
sentences.zh: 它们确实在聚集，因为在接下来的几天里，有传言称外省有军队在行军。

sentences.en: People are swapping stories and they're saying they've heard that there are tens of thousands
sentences.zh: 人们在交换着各种消息，他们说听说有数万名

sentences.en: of troops coming towards the capital from the frontier garrisons, and in particular, German and Swiss troops who fight for the French king.
sentences.zh: 军队从边境卫戍部队向首都进发，特别是为法国国王效力的德国和瑞士军队。

sentences.en: Mirabeau says, does the king doubt the loyalty of his people?
sentences.zh: 米拉波说，国王是在怀疑他的人民的忠诚吗？

sentences.en: And Louis has to issue a public statement saying, these troops are to reinforce the troops already in Paris, which are proving unreliable, which is true.
sentences.zh: 路易不得不发表公开声明称，这些军队是为了增援已经在巴黎、且事实证明不可靠的军队，这倒确有其事。

sentences.en: Well, the French guard in particular in Paris, there have been stories about them disobeying their officers, fraternising with looters, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特别是巴黎的法国卫队，有传言说他们不服从长官，与掠夺者称兄道弟，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And there is a sense, as more and more of these stories mount, that the crowds in Paris are getting ever more radical, the rhetoric ever more violent.
sentences.zh: 随着这类消息越来越多，人们感觉到巴黎的人群变得越来越激进，言辞也越来越暴力。

sentences.en: Early July, there's a story that the crowd sees as suspected police informants and they beat him to death.
sentences.zh: 七月初，有传言称人群发现了一个涉嫌警察线人的人，并把他活活打死。

sentences.en: There is this kind of latent simmering violence.
sentences.zh: 这种潜在的、暗流涌动的暴力情绪正在滋生。

sentences.en: And in Versailles, some of Louis' advisors say, sure, you gave in to the National Assembly the other day, but this is the last chance now.
sentences.zh: 在凡尔赛宫，路易的一些顾问说，没错，你前几天对国民议会妥协了，但这已经是最后的机会了。

sentences.en: We have to act.
sentences.zh: 我们必须采取行动。

sentences.en: This is the last opportunity we'll ever have to seize control of the situation.
sentences.zh: 这是我们夺回局势控制权的最后一次机会了。

sentences.en: Sack Necker.
sentences.zh: 解雇内克尔。

sentences.en: Put an end to all of this nonsense.
sentences.zh: 结束所有这些荒唐事。

sentences.en: Use these new troops from the frontiers to secure the city.
sentences.zh: 利用这些从边境调来的新军队来确保城市的安全。

sentences.en: The question is whether the army will obey orders.
sentences.zh: 问题在于军队是否会服从命令。

sentences.en: The royal commander, the Duke de Broglie, says it is risky.
sentences.zh: 皇家指挥官德·布罗伊公爵表示这很冒险。

sentences.en: He says, we don't have enough troops to secure all of Paris, to fight our way through all of
sentences.zh: 他说，我们的军队还不足以控制整个巴黎，不足以杀出一条血路穿过整个

sentences.en: Paris.
sentences.zh: 巴黎。

sentences.en: Other advisors say, so tellingly, get out of Versailles now.
sentences.zh: 其他顾问则意味深长地建议：现在就离开凡尔赛吧。

sentences.en: You know, you don't want to be a prisoner.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你可不想当阶下囚。

sentences.en: Let's go to Metz on the frontier out in Alsace.
sentences.zh: 让我们去阿尔萨斯边境的梅斯吧。

sentences.en: We're so close to foreign support.
sentences.zh: 我们离外国的支持很近。

sentences.en: We can get foreign aid if necessary.
sentences.zh: 如有必要，我们可以获得外国援助。

sentences.en: Paris is gone.
sentences.zh: 巴黎已经没救了。

sentences.en: But then other people say, no, we can't do that because if we abandon Paris now, we'll never get it back.
sentences.zh: 但另一些人则说，不，我们不能这么做，因为如果我们现在抛弃巴黎，就再也夺不回它了。

sentences.en: We'll be setting ourselves against the capital and we can't do that.
sentences.zh: 我们将与首都对立，这是我们做不到的。

sentences.en: Right, and a king leaving his own capital to go inside with foreign powers is not a good look.
sentences.zh: 没错，国王离开自己的首都去投靠外国势力，这可不是什么好名声。

sentences.en: And that is true now and it will be true in due course, as we will see.
sentences.zh: 现在如此，将来也必然如此，正如我们将会看到的。

sentences.en: Of course it is, Tom.
sentences.zh: 当然是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: It's so ominous, all of these conversations, because they're anticipating so much of what will follow.
sentences.zh: 所有这些对话都太不祥了，因为它们预示了后面发生的太多事情。

sentences.en: But anyway, Louis finally makes up his mind and he says, okay, I know what we'll do.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，路易终于下定决心说，好吧，我知道该怎么做了。

sentences.en: We'll go with your first idea.
sentences.zh: 我们就听你最初的想法。

sentences.en: So on the night of the 11th of July, the plan is set in motion.
sentences.zh: 所以在7月11日深夜，计划开始付诸实施。

sentences.en: Late that night, out of nowhere, Necker is dismissed.
sentences.zh: 那天深夜，毫无征兆地，内克尔被解职了。

sentences.en: Louis tells him, you're sacked.
sentences.zh: 路易告诉他，你被解雇了。

sentences.en: You are exiled from France.
sentences.zh: 你被驱逐出法国。

sentences.en: You have to leave the kingdom immediately and you cannot go through Paris.
sentences.zh: 你必须立即离开王国的领土，并且不准经由巴黎。

sentences.en: You cannot visit the capital.
sentences.zh: 你不准访问首都。

sentences.en: You can't stop on the way you must go to Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 你在途中不能停留，必须直奔瑞士。

sentences.en: A noble deputy called Gaston de Lévis, who knows all about this business, he sends a warning to his wife who's in the capital that night.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫加斯顿·德·莱维的贵族代表对这一切了如指掌，他当晚向身在首都的妻子发出了警告。

sentences.en: And the warning reads as follows.
sentences.zh: 警告内容如下。

sentences.en: Don't go out at all tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天千万不要出门。

sentences.en: There will surely be a dreadful commotion and one cannot know how things will go.
sentences.zh: 肯定会有可怕的骚乱，谁也不知道事情会变成什么样。

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, what a cliffhanger.
sentences.zh: 好了，多米尼克，真是个悬念迭起的地方。

sentences.en: The clock is ticking down towards one of the most famous dates in the whole, not just the
sentences.zh: 倒计时正在向整个（不仅仅是法国历史，甚至是）历史中最著名的日期之一迈

sentences.en: French history, but of history falls stopped.
sentences.zh: 进。

sentences.en: The 14th of July, 1789, the day the Bastille falls.
sentences.zh: 1789年7月14日，巴士底狱陷落的日子。

sentences.en: And we will be looking at that in our next episode.
sentences.zh: 我们将在下一集中探讨这个话题。

sentences.en: And if you can't wait, you know the drill.
sentences.zh: 如果你等不及了，你知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: You can hear it right now by joining the Restless History Club at therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过访问 therestishistory.com 加入“历史就是这样”俱乐部，现在就能收听。

sentences.en: But if you don't do that, it'll be coming very soon anyway.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不这么做，它也很快就会上线。

sentences.en: So we will see you soon.
sentences.zh: 所以我们很快就会再见。

sentences.en: A bientôt.
sentences.zh: 回头见。

sentences.en: Au revoir.
sentences.zh: 再见。
